complaints.text: I am formally disputing an erroneous move out charge of $450.00 for "BED WINDOW RPL" (bedroom window replacement) assessed to my account by REMOVEDon REMOVED(REMOVED, REMOVED). I lived in Unit REMOVEDD and officially moved out on July 31, 2026. For the entire summer leading up to my move out date, I was completely out of town, residing hundreds of miles away at my permanent home address. I had already completely cleared all of my personal belongings out of the bedroom prior to leaving the city, meaning the room was entirely vacant and empty during this period. On July 28, 2026, I became aware that a window in my vacant bedroom had been damaged. This damage was caused entirely by an outside social guest visiting the apartment while I was away. It was not caused by me or anyone under my direct authority. Because I was away and the room was empty, I had absolutely no control over who entered the apartment or how my vacant space was impacted. Despite being out of town, I acted with immediate urgency as a responsible tenant. I proactively submitted maintenance Service Request #REMOVEDon July 28, 2026, specifically so they could fix it right away and be alerted to the situation. The repair was completed by maintenance technician REMOVEDon August 4, 2026.American Campus Communities is wrongfully holding me financially liable for property damage caused entirely by a third party to an empty room while my absence from the city is completely documented. I filed a formal dispute via email to REMOVEDon September 2, 2026, but have received no response. Because the local leasing office states they lack the administrative authority to alter move out ledgers, I am trapped in an unresponsive loop while this unfair balance risks being sent to collections. I am asking corporate management to review the timeline, recognize my proactive reporting, and absolve this charge. I can provide documented proof of my summer absence upon request.
complaints.businessResponse:
Hello REMOVED,

We apologize for the stress and inconvenience this situation has caused. Your dispute was originally sent to the wrong email, unfortunately, and that is why we were not responsive. The correct email is BalanceDisputes@AmericanCampus.com.After reviewing the maintenance records, the technicians work order, and the move-out ledger, we have decided to waive the $450.00 charge for the bedroom window replacement.

What we are doing: 

The $450.00 BED WINDOW RPL charge will be removed from your account immediately.
Your account ledger will be updated to reflect this change and you will not be referred to collections concerning this item.
You will receive written confirmation of the charge removal once it is processed in the system.

We appreciate that you reported the damage promptly and cooperated in allowing maintenance to complete the repair. If you need any further documentation for your records or have additional questions, please contact our office at REMOVEDor REMOVED

Again,we apologize for any inconvenience this matter caused and thank you for bringing it to our attention.

Sincerely, 


*. REMOVED

U Club on REMOVEDProperty Manager

complaints.text: I am disputing charges on the final statement for The Cottages of REMOVED. This unit was rented for two consecutive years for my REMOVEDstudent. Upon move in it was noted that there was wall paint used to paint a section of the ceiling above the bed and there was a very poorly done patch on the bathroom wall to the left of the mirror. The walls were returned in EXACLTY the condition as they were when this lease started. There was absolutely NO signs of use wear or any damage to anything in this unit. The unit was meticulously cleaned and doors locked and keys returned in May of 2026. The lease was paid with no occupants until August. In August of 2026 a final bill was sent charging for $350.00 to paint the entire bedroom and $55.00 to paint the bathroom. A unit condition form was submitted at move in on August 25, 2024 and that information has been removed from the resident portal so that it can not be sent to you as proof. All other documentation is still available on the resident portal ie: leases, maintenance requests, vehicle info. I have submitted an online complaint with American Campus as well as called the local Cottages of REMOVED. I have also asked for REMOVEDof the property manager to return my call and was told she was too busy. A request for a Senior Manager from American Campus customer service to call me was also left. Neither have been able to give me a copy of my original unit condition form or any photos of damage or proof of work being performed to repair any damage. This type of erroneous charging is something that seems to be done quite frequently with this company.
complaints.businessResponse:
We apologize for the frustration you experienced while attempting to submit your dispute and access the Unit Condition Form. After confirming the appropriate dispute submission process,our team worked with you to troubleshoot the portal access issue, provided the available Unit Condition Form information, and submitted a request for technical support to restore access to the form and related photos. We also encouraged you to include any supporting documentation or photos with your dispute for consideration during the review.

Your dispute has been directed to the appropriate team for review, and we have asked that it be addressed as promptly as possible. We understand the importance of clear communication and access to relevant documentation, and we will continue monitoring the technical request and provide updates as information becomes available.

 

*. REMOVED

Property Manager

complaints.text: I am filing this complaint regarding an unsubstantiated move-out fee charged to my daughter and her roommates following the conclusion of their lease at REMOVEDin REMOVED, REMOVEDdaughter resided in this unit for over two years. Upon move-out, a full walk-through of the apartment was conducted, during which no visual damage to the furniture or unit was identified. Despite this, management subsequently issued an invoice demanding $1,500.00 from the tenants, vaguely alleging that the couch required replacement.This claim is improper and unreasonable for the following reasons:Lack of Evidence: Management provided zero photographic evidence, inspection reports, or detailed line-item justifications supporting the claim of damage prior to demanding payment. Standard landlord-tenant protocols require clear before-and-after photographic proof demonstrating tenant-caused damage beyond normal wear and tear.Normal Wear and Tear: Given the two-plus-year duration of tenancy, expected standard wear and tear does not constitute damage warranting full replacement costs billed to the tenants.Move-In Documentation: We possess photographic evidence documenting the condition of the furniture and unit at REMOVEDsomeone who works in the legal industry, I understand the necessity of due process and evidentiary support when asserting financial claims. Unsubstantiated claims reported to collection agencies or credit bureaus will be disputed vigorously, and we reserve all legal remedies available under Florida law should any false claims negatively impact my daughters, my wifes, or my credit standing.Desired Settlement / Resolution:Immediate dismissal and written zero-balance clearance of the $1,500.00 move-out invoice; OR Full photographic evidence (both before move-in and after move-out) along with a detailed, itemized proof of damage clearly establishing liability beyond normal wear and tear.
complaints.businessResponse:
Good morning, Mr. REMOVEDyou for reaching out to us regarding the charges on REMOVEDaccount. As we discussed, we have placed a request with our resident account team to have the charges for the blinds, love seat and front door removed as the photos that were submitted during the inspection do not justify the charges. As for the charge for the couch, this will remain on REMOVEDaccount as the photo our team submitted at the time of the move-out inspection displayed the couch being in poor condition, and we are unable to determine if this was the condition of the couch when REMOVEDinitially moved in as she did not complete a unit condition form for the apartment.

Please allow up to 48 hours for the removed charges to reflect on REMOVEDaccount. Please inform me if you have any further questions or concerns. Thank you. 

*. REMOVED

Resident Experience Manager

complaints.text: This business is deceiving. Earlier this year, took a tour to see their apartment complex for university student housing. The model unit shown was very nice. Granted, its a rental property, and expect a little wear in unit. However, upon moving in after paying 1st months rent, the unit was in grave condition. Doors not closing, bugs everywhere, spider webs everywhere., kitchen sink falling through to the cabinet space below, smelly, hole in window, very filthy. With renting an apartment, the facility owner is to provide a clean unit that is safe and clean for habitation. This was not and borders on being unsafe for healthy occupation. But to make matters worse, the facilitys office is closed a few hours after move in time and the day after (Saturday move in at noon assigned time and Sunday is next day) for a very large complex for university students. The owner REMOVEDisnt holding up their end of the lease to provide a healthy. Cleaned, functional living space to a new renter. I will visually inspect for mold and mildew and will contact local health department if seen. This company also fails to provide support to new renters on assigned and only move in weekend
complaints.businessResponse:
Following a review of our records, the property team was unable to identify any prior reports or escalations from the residents regarding these concerns before the BBB complaint was submitted.

Management has since spoken with both the resident and their parent to discuss the concerns and apologize for the residents initial move-in experience and the inconvenience caused. As of August 24, 2026, all reported issues have been resolved, and management has followed up with the resident and parent to confirm their satisfaction with the resolution. Management also encouraged the resident to contact the leasing office with any future questions or concerns so they may be addressed promptly.


*. REMOVED

Director/Property Management

complaints.text: I am disputing two unsupported move-out charges assessed by REMOVEDBinghamton after I moved out on July 31, 2026: a fire alarm charge and a $50 bed cleaning charge.I first disputed these directly with REMOVED. They replied that the property could not override move-out charges and directed me to American Campus Communities disputes process. They also provided supposed photo evidence, but it does not support the charges against me.Our apartment previously had malfunctioning fire alarms that rang without cause. We reported this, and REMOVEDmaintenance entered the unit and worked on/replaced alarms. We did not remove or alter them ourselves.The fire alarm photo REMOVEDprovided is not from my bedroom. It is from the common area near my roommates' rooms, and they continued living in the apartment after I moved out. More importantly, REMOVEDmaintenance had previously worked on these alarms and left them in their existing condition. I did not remove, damage, or tamper with any alarm.I have a timestamped July 31 move-out photo showing the fire alarm in my own bedroom. REMOVEDhas provided no evidence that the alarm in my room was damaged or missing.I also dispute the $50 bed cleaning charge. The REMOVEDmattress was protected by a mattress protector, a roughly four-inch latex topper with its own cover, and additional bedding. I have timestamped move-out photos showing the mattress protection still in place and us removing the covered topper immediately before leaving.Despite charging me for bed cleaning, REMOVEDprovided no photo of my bed or mattress showing any stain, dirt, damage, or condition requiring cleaning. I asked what specifically required cleaning and why I was charged $50, but no supporting evidence/explanation was provided.I am requesting that both charges be removed. If REMOVEDbelieves either is valid, I request specific evidence showing the condition attributed to me, why I am responsible for it, and how the amount was determined.

BED TRASH OUT/BAG CLN                       $50.00

complaints.text: My daughter lives in this community and has for the past three years. Her air conditioning has went out several times in the middle of summer. Temps inside have reached the high 80s. Maintenance was either slow to come out or had to come out several times as it would stop working right away. If the temp is above 80 degrees that is considered emergent but they do not come out right away as if its emergent. She has went several days with no ac at times. The front desk told her they cant make maintenance come out A couple weeks ago her digital key stopped working and her physical key also wasnt working. She was locked out at 12 am called the emergency line and no one answered. Someone was in the parking lot screaming. Security came out to investigate and she waved him over for help. He tried calling the maintenance line no response. She called every few minutes for hours. No response. We live 3 hours away and she had to work in the morning so couldnt really come home and had nowhere else to go. Finally about 3 hours later she thought to delete the app and reinstall and her key re appeared. But she was outside for all those hours waiting on this nonexistent emergency line. They finally called back 730a. I just wonder what wouldve happened if she hadnt reinstalled her app. Would she have been stuck outside all night. Very unsafe. All of her roommates had moved out the prior week so no one inside to let her in. I emailed the corporate office as well as the front office. The front office only said sorry and that they would forward my email. Hadnt heard anything else. I called the corporate line last week and someone took my complaint but havent heard anything else. No one has responded to my concerns at all. The last time my daughters air went out she called the corporate number and they couldnt get anyone on the phone either. On the website they advertise 24hr emergency response this is false advertising because it does not exist.
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for providing additional context regarding your experience. We understand your frustration with the recurring HVAC concerns and the difficulty you experienced obtaining assistance during your lockout. We are glad your HVAC is currently operating properly and that the most recent service request, submitted on August 14, was completed that same day. HVAC concerns remain a priority, particularly when apartment temperatures become elevated,and residents are encouraged to contact the office directly regarding unresolved or urgent maintenance concerns.

We also recognize that the response you received during your late-night lockout did not meet expectations. The circumstances surrounding the missed calls have been addressed with the team member involved, who also apologized directly the following day. We appreciate you bringing these concerns to our attention, as your feedback helps us identify opportunities to improve our processes. Your concerns have been documented, and we remain available to assist directly with any recurring or significant issues moving forward.

J REMOVED

Resident Experience Manager

complaints.text: My daughter moved into Callaway House REMOVEDearly this year (8/15/26) so that she could participate in sorority rush. She is in a 4x4 unit which means she has her own bathroom and bedroom. When we arrived her sink was actively leaking underneath, and it appears it had been like this for some time as the vanity cabinet was warped. After multiple calls to the emergency maintenance line someone came up to turn off the water and then said they would return the next day to replace the entire sink and vanity. Today is day 4 and she still has no functioning sink. I have sent multiple emails and opened several tickets to no avail. I have asked for someone to return my call but no one will. The facilities manager emailed me and said that since she has access to a sink (ie THE KITCHEN SINK) we would not qualify for a Prorated refund. complaints.text: Apartment Complex Name: REMOVEDFull Address: REMOVEDResident Unit Number: Unit 422 COMPLAINT DETAILS:This complaint is regarding unfair business practices, inconsistent policy enforcement, and preferential treatment at REMOVEDOn Friday, July 17th, I went to the front desk to request a mobile key fob. The on-duty staff denied my request, claiming property policy strictly mandates that residents can only hold either a physical key fob or a mobile fob, but never both. However, my roommate A currently possesses both active fobs. This is part of a pattern of inconsistent and unfair rule enforcement. Previously, I was locked out of my room and instructed by the after-hours on-call staff that I was required to pay a lockout fee. Conversely, my roommate B had her lockout fee completely waived by the staff under identical circumstances my roommate B informed me that her lockout fee was waived by a staff member who is her personal friend. Local management is failing to enforce community policies uniformly. Staff are utilizing their positions to grant preferential treatment to personal friends while enforcing financial penalties and technological restrictions on other paying residents. This creates an unfair, unequal, and unprofessional housing environment. I have already attempted to resolve this matter directly by emailing the apartment. However, the response I received was unsatisfactory and didnt address the inconsistency in policy enforcement. I request that this issue gets resolved in one of two ways to ensure fair treatment: either instruct the local Grandmarc Seven Corners team to issue me an active mobile key fob so my access privileges match my roommate's, or strictly reinforce the "one fob only" policy across all residents uniformly, which includes revoking one form of access for current residents that has dual access.

I currently live at the province REMOVED, which is a student housing facility, included in our rent per our resident handbook is our Wi-Fi charges. The past three weeks there has been no Wi-Fi. I have tried to get in contact with the managers and they have not contacted me back. I have reached out in regards to some type of compensation or credit back to our account since we are paying for a service that we are not able to have access to for going on three weeks now. the managing staff has continued to ignore me and says they are working on the issue, but I do not see it getting actively fixed. They are not offering any residence a credit of any sort or compensation for hotspots and suggesting we use the clubhouse which has one single study room and we are currently in an active semester of class. I also have chronic autoimmune disease which constricts me from being able to do my assignments or schoolwork, which is why I usually do my schoolwork in my room because I have been paying for Wi-Fi, going to the public library and clubhouse is not a feasible option due to my medical issues. I have documentation of all emails sent on my behalf and the apartment. I also have the resident handbook where it states we pay for our WI-FI in our rent.
complaints.businessResponse: REMOVED,thank you for taking the time to share your feedback. We understand how frustrating the recent internet outage was and appreciate your patience while the issue was being addressed. Following the weather-related outage, our onsite management team worked closely with our internet service provider to restore service as quickly as possible. Since service has been restored, we have had the opportunity to speak with you directly and discuss your experience. We are continuing to work with you on the remaining items we discussed and will provide updates as they become available.We remain committed to providing timely communication as we work toward a resolution.

complaints.text: I have a $1500 REMOVEDwasher dryer. I have warranty through CPS I have made 2 plus calls to CPS. No one can or wants to work on this machine. The its going on 3 months since this machine has worked . Every time I call cps i get the run around. They disconnect my calls . CPS told me I need to find a person to fix the machine and I can find anyone just like they can't find someone to fix it. I spent $99 to have someone fix this machine that is what cps charged me. This company is useless and their mission statement is a lie.
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for forwarding this complaint. CPS has reviewed REMOVEDfile and offers the following response.
Upon receipt of REMOVEDclaim, CPS worked to locate an authorized servicer able to handle the reported issue. Service availability in REMOVEDarea is limited, and the type of appliance involved narrows the pool of qualified providers further. We approached several service centers in the region.
The claim was assigned to REMOVED, the servicer in the area equipped to work on this unit. REMOVEDwas booked out and could not schedule the repair within a reasonable window. CPS subsequently attempted to reassign the claim back to REMOVEDonce availability improved. Following an interaction between REMOVEDand that service center, Wilco advised CPS that they were not willing to continue working with him on this claim.
With no other authorized servicer available in the area, CPS also extended REMOVEDthe option of obtaining a repair estimate from an independent provider of his choosing and submitting it to us for approval. He advised that he was unable to locate a provider willing to perform the work.
Given that no service could be secured through any available channel, CPS refunded REMOVEDthe deductible he paid on this claim rather than leave it open indefinitely. That refund has been issued.
We would also note for the record that REMOVEDservice contract has since reached the end of its term and is expired. No further claims can be filed under it.
CPS considers the deductible refund to be the appropriate resolution in this matter.

complaints.text: My husband and I purchased a policy for our new air conditioner in Feb 2026 from Consumer Priority Service. We chose the unit because it was supposed to help with humidity and we live around a lake. In April, we started monitoring the humidity. It wasnt low. My husband asked me to place a call to see if anyone could take a look to make sure everything was working ok. I did so. Then he told me to cancel it because he found a number where he could talk to someone with ACIQ. We ultimately determined the system was fine, but we had to install a whole home dehumidifier. Instead of cancelling the claim, it was denied. On REMOVED22, 2026 my husband and I came home and the REMOVEDwas not working. He did troubleshoot the issue and gave me notes to relay to the Consumer Priority Service. I called to place a claim. I have explained the situation multiple times. I keep getting placed back on hold. Today I have been on hold for 3.5 hours total. I have asked for a manager, but they just keep saying one will call me. While on hold the lines starts to ring and it is placed back on hold. They are telling me that I cannot place another claim until I prove to them that we had the humidity issue fixed. There wasnt an issue. The claim should have been cancelled. The policy we received states that you can resubmit for a new claim at any time, but if the claim is related to a previously denied claim you must provide proof it was fixed. We never had anyone come fix an issue. We paid $469.99 for this policy. We feel they are not being ethical.
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for forwarding this matter. We have reviewed the customer's file and offer the following.

REMOVEDpurchased a service agreement covering her air conditioning unit in February 2026. In April 2026, she contacted us reporting that the unit was not adequately controlling humidity. That claim was reviewed and denied. Failures or performance deficiencies existing at or near the time of purchase fall to the manufacturer's warranty and the selling dealer's return policy, not to the extended service agreement.

On August 22, 2026, REMOVEDsubmitted a new claim on the same unit. Her service agreement provides that a claim may be resubmitted at any time, but where the new claim relates to a previously denied claim, documentation confirming the prior condition was repaired must be provided. Our representatives requested that documentation. REMOVEDadvised that no repair was performed. Absent that documentation, we are unable to verify that the current condition is separate from the previously denied matter, and the claim remains under review rather than approved.

We are prepared to move forward promptly. If REMOVEDcan provide any technician report, invoice, or written assessment addressing the unit's condition following the April contact including documentation from the manufacturer regarding the dehumidifier installation we will review the August claim on its merits without further delay.

We also acknowledge the customer's account of extended hold times and an unreturned supervisor request. That experience does not meet our standard and has been raised with our call center management.

We remain willing to work with REMOVEDtoward a resolution and can be reached directly at the contact information on file.

The head rests also stopped functioning to. They advertised accidental damage like spills and stains as well. It had some spills and stains and we used professional cleaners to handle it but eventually that stopped working. We finally made the claim and they came out claiming "misuse" and denied the claim. This is clearly a measure taken to not honor there plan and a failure to stand behind there product the original purchase was for and extended warranty that included accidental, manufacturing defects, and stains. I just want my couch fixed and its unacceptable that they have failed to respond to my attempts at getting further investigation into this. Its a minor deal im not asking for much. They have the warranty I purchased it. If they cant honor it and lie about stuff to steal from consumers then they should not be able to sell warranties. I want a resolution on this please. It has been a massive waste of my time which is frustrating.
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for forwarding this complaint. We have reviewed REMOVEDfile in full and would like to provide the following clarification.

REMOVEDpurchased a furniture protection plan in 2021 in connection with his sofa. A claim was submitted in 2025, and in accordance with our standard procedure we dispatched an independent, factory-authorized technician to inspect the furniture on site and document the reported conditions. The technician's findings identified misuse, accumulated wear and tear, and excessive physical damage to the product. These conditions are specifically excluded under the terms and conditions of the plan, which were provided to REMOVEDat the time of purchase. On that basis, the claim was denied.

With respect to the manufacturing defect REMOVEDdescribes, he states that the springs began failing within the first two years of ownership. Defects arising in that period fall under the manufacturer's warranty, which runs concurrent with and takes precedence over our coverage. Our plan also does not extend to conditions that pre-date the coverage period or to progressive damage that went unreported at the time it occurred. Had the spring failure been reported when REMOVEDfirst observed it, it would have been directed to the manufacturer for resolution.

Regarding the accidental stain coverage, the plan covers single-incident accidental spills and stains reported within the timeframe specified in the terms and conditions. It does not cover cumulative soiling, general soil buildup, or the deterioration of the fabric over multiple years of use. REMOVEDown description confirms repeated staining addressed through professional cleaning over an extended period, which falls outside the scope of what the plan is designed to cover.

We want to be clear that our determination is based entirely on the documented inspection findings and the plan language, not on any unwillingness to honor the coverage REMOVEDpurchased.

complaints.text: REMOVEDwarranty was purchased with purchase of an induction stove in November of 2022. Control board failed in 2026. Warranty claim was filed with CPS for coverage of replacement part ($856) under the warranty, which was initially denied and denied again on appeal. The warranty expressly provides for coverage of "Bake/Broil & Surface Elements" of an electric range. On an induction range (a type of electric range), the surface element consists of the induction system. Without the power module, the surface element cannot function -- the control board and inverter are functionally tied to the surface element. Without the board, the copper coils cannot generate a magnetic field; this failure is preventing the surface element from operating. CPS acknowledges that major components are covered under MAC10, but somehow refuses to acknowledge that the control board (an $800+ part) is a major component.
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for forwarding this complaint. We have reviewed REMOVEDfile, including the original claim determination and the subsequent appeal, and we are upholding the denial.
REMOVEDpurchased a REMOVEDAppliance Component warranty in November 2022. This is a limited, parts-only warranty. It is not a comprehensive service contract and it does not cover the appliance as a whole. Coverage is limited to the specific major components enumerated in the terms and conditions. Parts not listed are excluded, and the terms state this expressly.
The part REMOVEDsubmitted for coverage is the control board. A control board is a separate, individually identified component.  
REMOVEDposition is that because the surface element cannot operate without the control board, the control board must be covered as part of the surface element. Coverage under this warranty is defined by the failed part, not by the symptom the failure produces. Nearly every component in a modern appliance is functionally necessary to the operation of some other component; adopting that reasoning would extend a limited component warranty to the entire unit and would render the enumerated component list meaningless. That is not the coverage that was sold or purchased.
We also want to address the characterization that CPS "refuses to acknowledge that the control board is a major component." Cost is not the standard. The REMOVEDwarranty does not cover parts on the basis of price; it covers the specific components named in the contract. An expensive part that is not listed remains outside the scope of coverage, just as an inexpensive listed part remains within it.
REMOVEDclaim received a full review at the time of filing and a second-level review on appeal. Both reached the same conclusion. Accordingly, we are unable to reimburse the $856.00 cost of the control board, and no refund is owed on the claim.

complaints.text: I purchased a repair plan warranty (#REMOVED) on 3/19/26 from Consumer Priority Service. Our refrigerator quit cooling mid-June and I filed a claim (REMOVED) on 6/30/26. CPS contacted me on 7/24/26 and assigned a company to my claim and asked me to contact them to set up a time for them to diagnose the refrigerator. They were scheduled to come out on 7/3/26, but they didn't show. I emailed CPS on that day to let them know. They rescheduled them to come back on 7/10/26. Again, they didn't show. I contacted REMOVEDKneeler twice that day to inform her he didn't show. I didn't hear back from her until 7/17/26. She said give her til Monday 7/19/26. I heard back on 7/21/26 to inform me another company was assigned to my claim, and I needed to set up a time for them to come out. They came out on 7/23/26 and diagnosed the refrigerator as a seal system problem. We received an email from CPS stating they are having a hard time finding someone to fix my refrigerator and I needed to find a 3rd company to come out and diagnose the refrigerator, because SC Appliance Repair stated they couldn't give them an estimate because the cost could vary from$200-3,000. I contacted HLC Handyman Service who came out on 8/6/26. He gave the same diagnosis as the first company. An email was sent to CPS stating that he could take a closer look for an additional $300. We received an email on 8/11/26 stating that CPS could not cover the $300 but could allow $150 for deeper diagnostic testing. Consumer Priority is not fulfilling their contract obligations, as they have rejected 2 diagnosis and will not pay to have my refrigerator repaired. Our maximum coverage allowance is $3500. Warranty Details state "We offer free repair coverage for your product any time during the life of your warranty. If we can't fix it, we will replace it!" They are expecting me to pay for further diagnostics when contract specifically says they offer free repair coverage! 7 weeks now with no resolution!
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for forwarding this complaint. We have reviewed claim #REMOVEDunder warranty #REMOVEDin full.
REMOVEDfiled her claim on 6/30/26 for a refrigerator that had stopped cooling. A servicer was assigned and, after two missed appointments by that provider, we reassigned the claim to a second servicer who inspected the unit on 7/23/26 and identified a sealed system failure. That servicer advised us that it could not provide a repair estimate, citing a potential cost range of $200 to $3,000. Because we cannot authorize a repair without a defined scope and cost, a third provider, HLC Handyman Service, inspected the unit on 8/6/26 and confirmed the same diagnosis but likewise did not furnish a repair estimate, instead quoting an additional $300 for further teardown and testing. We authorized $150 toward that additional diagnostic work.
We acknowledge that the delays in scheduling the initial service visits fell short of the level of service we expect to provide, and we regret the inconvenience this caused. To address that, we have reimbursed REMOVEDfor her out-of-pocket service call cost, and that reimbursement was processed on 8/24/26.
REMOVEDplan provides for repair or replacement up to a limit of liability of $3,500, and that coverage remains fully intact. What is required to move forward is a complete repair estimate identifying the failed components and the labor cost to correct them. Once that estimate is submitted to us, we will review it promptly for authorization and issue payment for the covered repair up to the plan's limit of liability. If a repair cannot be completed, we will address the claim under the replacement provisions of the agreement. No portion of the covered repair cost is being passed to REMOVEDask that REMOVEDforward the completed estimate to her claims contact at her earliest convenience so that we can finalize authorization. We remain available to assist with locating an additional servicer if that would be helpful.

complaints.text: purchased a refrigerator in December 2023 with an extended warranty administered by Consumer Priority Service CPS About one month later, the ice maker stopped working. I contacted CPS and was told it was a self-fix issue. I followed the instructions, but it still did not work. I contacted CPS again and was again instructed to attempt a self-repair. That was also unsuccessful.I later submitted another claim and received no meaningful follow-up until I contacted CPS again myself.CPS eventually sent a technician, who determined that the ice maker required replacement. He attempted the repair but was unable to remove the ice maker from the refrigerator and could not complete the repair. His findings were submitted to CPS.Afterward, I contacted CPS requesting either a successful repair or replacement if the refrigerator could not reasonably be repaired.On August 3, 2026, CPS advised me in writing that REMOVEDwas being added to my claim as the claims liaison to expedite my request and asked her to contact me. I received no communication from her.I followed up again on August 5.On August 6, REMOVEDemailed me stating that CPS had flagged my account for review, identified herself as the Relationship Manager assigned to my account, and stated that CPS would review the account over the next 24 hours and determine the best available resolution.That timeframe expired without any call, email, repair authorization, replacement decision, or REMOVEDof August 10, I am still waiting for CPS to resolve a refrigerator problem I first reported shortly after purchase.I have complied with CPSs troubleshooting requests, made the appliance available for inspection and repair, and repeatedly followed up when communication REMOVEDcomplaint is that CPS has failed to provide a timely and effective resolution under the extended warranty after its own technician determined that the ice maker required replacement and was unable to complete the repair.
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for the opportunity to respond, and we apologize for the delays and the gaps in follow-up you experienced on this claim.
Our technician confirmed the ice maker requires replacement and attempted that repair on site. He was unable to complete it because the ice maker assembly cannot be removed from the refrigerator. That obstruction is a design condition of the unit itself it is not a failure of the part, and it is not something a further dispatch would resolve. The ice maker is the only reported issue; the refrigerator is otherwise operating normally.
Our service agreement covers mechanical and electrical failures that occur during normal use. It does not cover design defects or conditions inherent to the manufacture of the product. Because the condition preventing this repair is a design issue with the refrigerator, it falls outside the terms of coverage, and we are unable to authorize a repair or replacement on that basis.
We recommend contacting the manufacturer directly regarding the design condition, as this is an issue with the product's construction rather than a covered breakdown. We're happy to provide our technician's report to support that conversation.

They state that CPS may offer a replacement of like kind and function or a monetary settlement equal to the current market value (CMV) of the covered product.I repeatedly asked CPS to explain how it calculated the value, identify the comparable products or other data used to establish CMV, and explain the contractual basis for its valuation. I recalled it as approximately $130, while CPS has since told me it was approximately $120. The subsequent offer was $119. CPS has the records showing the exact amounts.I am not seeking anything beyond the coverage I purchased. I want CPS to honor the protection plan by replacing the failed device with a comparable device or providing a settlement supported by the contract and an actual, documented current-market-value calculation.

complaints.text: In January 2020 I purchased a Frigidaire Gallery refrigerator (Model FG4H2272UF) for $2,049.00 and a CPS 5-Year Extended Warranty (#REMOVED) for $199.00. The refrigerator failed repeatedly. I filed three warranty claims (#REMOVED, #REMOVED, #REMOVED) between February and April 2024 for the same continuing failures ice maker, freezer temperature, and control board failure. CPS's own service provider, All County Appliance, confirmed in writing January 2025 that required parts were discontinued and the unit could not be repaired.CPS offered only a $199.00 premium refund citing parts unavailability, ignoring the No Lemon Policy in the same contract requiring replacement or cash settlement after three repairs for the same problem. CPS also sold me a renewal warranty in November 2024 using "If We Can't Fix It, We Replace It" language while refusing to honor that guarantee on my open claim.I sent a formal demand letter delivered March 4, 2025. CPS never responded in sixteen months. A second and final demand was delivered July 20, 2026 via REMOVEDCertified Mail (#REMOVED) demanding $3,159.38. CPS has still not responded. I ask the BBB to require full payment of $3,159.38 and investigate CPS's pattern of denying legitimate No Lemon claims.
complaints.businessResponse:
Consumer Priority Service has reviewed the above-referenced complaint and submits the following response.
REMOVEDpurchased a five-year extended service contract for her Frigidaire Gallery refrigerator at a premium of $199.00. Three claims were filed under the contract in 2024. In the course of servicing the unit, our authorized servicer, All County Appliance, determined that the components required to complete the repair are no longer available from the manufacturer and have been discontinued.
The contract addresses this circumstance directly. Where a covered failure cannot be repaired because required parts are no longer manufactured or otherwise unavailable, the contract provides that the plan is fulfilled by refund of the premium paid. That remedy was offered to REMOVEDand remains available to her.
The No Lemon provision REMOVEDcites operates differently. It applies where three separate covered repairs for the same defective component have been completed under the contract and a fourth failure of that same component occurs. The claims filed in 2024 concerned distinct components ice maker, temperature performance, and control board and no repair was completed on the third claim, because the parts required to perform it no longer exist. The No Lemon provision is therefore not triggered, and the parts-unavailability provision governs the outcome.
Contract #REMOVEDis a separate agreement with its own terms and effective period. Its purchase in November 2024 did not alter, extend, or supersede the terms of contract #REMOVED, and it does not create a replacement obligation with respect to a claim adjudicated under the prior contract.
The settlement amount demanded, $3,159.38, has no basis in either contract. Our liability under any service contract is capped by its terms and, in a parts-unavailability resolution, is limited to the premium paid.
Consumer Priority Service is prepared to issue the $199.00 premium refund upon REMOVEDconfirmation and will process it promptl

reviews.name: Cas C
reviews.text: I have booked through booking.com on multiple occasions and didn't have any issues. I recently booked through them again for a one night stay on our way home during a road trip. After driving for more than 8 hours, we get to the hotel and check in with no issues. We go to the room and notice an off smell. The whole room smelled like mold. In the bathroom, there was a significant amount of mold on the ceiling and the bathroom fan did not work. We were only staying one night and figured we could deal if we kept the bathroom door shut and checked out early. We ended up coughing all night. Nobody was at the front desk during checkout for us to mention the mold. After I returned from this stay, I contacted booking.com to receive a refund for the HEALTH HAZARD of a stay they recommended. Not only did customer service not help at all, one of the REMOVEDattempted to connect me to a manager only to hangup on me. Absolutely terrible customer service. I finally get through to a normal person in customer service who explained that they would have to reach out to the hotel to confirm. I didn't know what they needed to confirm (and me asking what they needed to confirm was never clarified due to language barriers) with the hotel since I had video and photographic proof of the condition of the room but I said ok. Its been 4 days and they finally get back to me via email stating that they were "unable to reach an agreement with the accommodation". Instead of a refund, they gave me $11 of credit. The hotel room was over $150 for the night.

reviews.name: Kent M
reviews.text: Beware! I am feeling extra stupid and idiotic in attempting to book a hotel room using this site (note, actually out of REMOVED!). THIS BUSINESS DOES NOT HAVE A CUSTOMER SERVICE PHONE NUMBER!If a problem were to arise, as it did with me, all I could do was email my complaint and concern...unsurprisingly, to no avail.Last week I needed to book a hotel room at the REMOVED, REMOVED. I foolishly proceeded with the (attempt at) booking a room, unaware that it was with this site called "booking.com" which, while it is no excuse, proved to be some kind of a fraud. At the end of the booking, and entering a credit card payment, I received something of an error message telling me that the payment was unable to be made. So, needing a room that very day, I pivoted to a different hotel in the same area. At the end of THAT process, I again received that odd notice that the payment could not be processed. To be fair (as if booking.com is!), the site said "non-refundable" payments. Of course, seeing the notification that my payment could not be processed, I figured that I was ok, in the clear so to speak. Imagine my surprise when my credit card was dinged THREE times, for three separate bookings on the same day. STAY FAR, FAR AWAY FROM THESE SCOUNDRELS

reviews.name: Aanchal K
reviews.text: Booking Ref: REMOVEDAug 1315, 2026 Amount: $780.42 I am filing this complaint against Booking.com for facilitating false advertising and failing to protect consumers from predatory bait-and-switch tactics.I booked a family stay at REMOVEDI self check-in" through Booking.com for a total of $780.42. I selected this specific room solely because the listing explicitly advertised Air Conditioning.Upon arriving with young children during a severe summer heatwave, we found the room had absolutely no AC. The hotel admitted this but refused to honor the Booking.com listing, instead using their local German website to justify the missing amenity. Their only "solution" was demanding an extra surcharge to split our family into two separate, smaller rooms. This was an unsafe, completely unacceptable alternative for a family. We refused this bait-and-switch, did not use the room, the bathroom, or any facilities, and immediately left. This ordeal forced us to waste hours of our vacation finding and paying completely out-of-pocket for last-minute accommodations in the heat.I immediately contacted Booking.com and provided timestamped screenshots of my booking. During multiple calls, Booking.com's own agents reviewed the evidence, checked the live listing, and explicitly agreed the room was falsely advertised with AC on their platform.Despite acknowledging this deception, Booking.com refused to secure a full refund for the $780.42. They claimed that because the hotel charged my card directly, they could only refund their commission as a REMOVEDEUR travel credit. I formally rejected this unacceptable offer.Booking.com cannot advertise amenities, facilitate a booking, and then wash its hands of responsibility when a customer is defrauded by blaming the vendor's billing process. I expect Booking.com to take responsibility for the false advertising on its platform and I request a full refund of $780.42.

On July 12, 2026 I booked a non-refundable hotel stay through my account on REMOVED. Because of my account benefits (Genius Tier 1 and VIP), I was offered the price of $308.07. I have a PDF printed from the website showing this price. Their FAQ page states "How are Genius rewards applied? Genius discounts and rewards are automatically applied to eligible stays and rental cars. No need for codes!" When the credit card notification came through after the booking, it showed the full price, not including the discounts, of $354.30. Their website malfunctioned. This is $46.23 higher than I agreed to. I immediately called booking.com and was told they couldn't process the refund without doing a price comparison, which would need to be reviewed, but assured me I would hear from them by email that day (yesterday, July 12, 2026). I didn't hear from them yesterday. Tonight I called to check on the refund. Without me agreeing to it, the agent credited my booking.com account with a $46.23 credit that is only "Valid on all bookings that accept Wallet payments" (I don't know which places do and which don't) and expires. Having a credit that is only good at booking.com and expires isn't as useful as having that refunded to the credit card used so that money can be spent elsewhere without expiration. Their website had a bug and I should not be paying more because of it. I want the refund, not the travel credit.
Customer Answer

Date: 08/16/2026

Better Business Bureau:

At this time, I have not been contacted by Booking.com USA, Inc. regarding complaint ID REMOVED.

Sincerely,

REMOVED

Company:Booking.com?Transaction date: Feb 17, 2026?Amount: $2,540.79 CAD?Service: Hotel reservation in REMOVED, Mar 1117, 2026, booked through Booking.com Booking.com is refusing to refund $2,540.79 CAD despite holding the funds and having explicit hotel approval. On Mar 11, 2026, one guest was denied entry to the REMOVEDdue to a name issue, preventing use of the reservation. On the same day, I contacted Booking.com. A Booking.com agent joined a call with the hotel reservations manager, who verbally approved a full refund with no cancellation penalty, and this confirmation is in Booking.com recordings. The hotel also provided written confirmation and a waiver on Mar 1112, 2026, which I submitted. Booking.com acknowledged receipt and confirmed the case was under review.Booking.com states refunds are subject to property approval, yet the hotel approved the refund verbally and in writing and Booking.com has still not issued it. The reservation remains active, and the case has been repeatedly delayed. Booking.com initially refused the cancellation, claiming REMOVED's system recorded the request as Mar 12, 2026 Asia time, after the hotel cancellation deadline. However, the booking terms specify deadlines are based on hotel local time HST, making the system time irrelevant. This refusal contradicts the contract. The hotel manager also disagreed with Booking.coms stated reason during the recorded call.I provided direct contact for the hotel Area Director of Reservations, screenshots of email waiver. Booking.com is the merchant of record and holds the funds. The hotel confirms they did not retain payment and authorized the refund on Mar 11, 2026. Attempting to shift responsibility does not relieve Booking.com of its contractual obligations. I have submitted confirmations, participated in a joint call, provided hotel contact info, and followed up multiple times since Mar 11, 2026, but the issue remains unresolved.Desired resolution: full refund of $2,540.79 CAD

reviews.name: Sarah G
reviews.text: I was told one 9-13-26 that i needed to verify my identity right away or I would be banned. I submitted my photo ID and was immediately told I was banned for good. A human did not verify my identity. I believed I was hacked and ultimately banned for life. This is so unacceptable and I am unable to receive any help. It wont let me appeal it again since it automatically said I was denied. Someone has to be able to help.

reviews.name: Tammy H
reviews.text: REMOVEDpermanently deleted my account of 16 years. Appealed was denied and cannot appeal again. There is no phone number or email for real customer support.

reviews.name: Tracy L
reviews.text: I am filing this complaint regarding REMOVED's business support process for a Facebook Business Manager and Page security incident that has gone unresolved for an extended period, actively damaging my small business.On August 21, 2026, an unauthorized individual gained access to my Meta Business Manager and removed my administrative access to my business Facebook Page, "Mai Autumn Decor." I immediately reported this and have since managed multiple case numbers for what should be one connected issue: Throughout this process: (1) I have been repeatedly misidentified as "REMOVED," the previous business owner; (2) the same issue has been split across four case numbers with no coordination between agents; (3) after confirming my availability multiple times, a scheduled phone call resulted in being told my case couldn't be resolved because "too many days" had passed, with no explanation or alternative offered; (4) one case was closed for "no correspondence received" despite my having replied; (5) someone referencing my specific case number contacted me offering to fix my access issue only if I paid them directly a possible sign of internal data exposure or misuse; (6) I have suffered significant ongoing financial harm from being unable to access or advertise on my Page for over a week.I am requesting Meta restore my full admin access to my Business Manager and Page, investigate how my case number was exposed, and improve its support process.

reviews.name: Erin C
reviews.text: From neat little website to neat little nightmare. Facebook personal page, public business page, Meta Business Suite, Business Portfolio, Ads Manager, Ads Dashboard... WHY does this require 6 systems? If not more.Absolutely ridiculous. You can be the main admin for a page and still be forbidden access. You can do everything the Meta Help Bot tells you to do, only to be sent in circles over and REMOVEDhas been over a week, and I have yet to connect with a live representative. Every attempt tells me they are too busy. Are there even live representatives at this point?I stopped our ads because after doing everything correctly, making the recommended adjustments, and trying to optimize the campaign, we got 0 leads. None. Now I can't even access every aspect of the account I am supposed to manage. We are service based, which makes things more difficult.If Facebook were brand new today, I would not recommend it to anyone. If I didn't need it for work, my account would be deleted.I also have an old personal account that I accidentally reactivated. I was able to log in from desktop several times over a few days, then suddenly Facebook stopped letting me access it. It remains active but inaccessible. All I wanted was to transfer some old photos. Now I can't even deactivate it.The amount of time I've wasted following Meta's instructions, troubleshooting access issues, and trying to find an actual person who can help is unbelievable.This is the worst customer service experience I have ever had. The worst experience with a website, period. Can't even leave a 'proper' review even though... Facebook is absolutely a business that PROVIDES and we should be able to leave reviews on Facebook on the page, on REMOVED, not just BBB.

reviews.name: Roger W
reviews.text: Got banned from FB marketplace for no reason. Can't speak to anyone about it. What an absolutely horrible system.

reviews.name: bone s
reviews.text: I am just trying to get my ad account activated but it says I am permanently banned and I can't figure out why. Please help!

reviews.name: mohamed a
reviews.text: "Following the latest application update, multiple personal accounts logged on my device were simultaneously and abruptly suspended. The system falsely and baselessly accused the accounts of violating standards regarding child sexual exploitation and abuse (CSAE), which is completely untrue. This automated mass-banning of independent accounts on a single device lacks any valid cause, human review, or a fair appeals process, causing severe distress and unfair restriction of consumer access."

reviews.name: Jennifer F
reviews.text: My husband has a substantial following on Facebook, and we spend a lot of money on REMOVEDads for our business. Meta's support is horrific, tossing you around and leaving issues unresolved. An AI inaccuracy prevented our account from monetizing for 10 months during his largest growth period, where we missed out on a minimum of $20k, upwards of $80k. Finally our Meta verification went through an we started earning. But Meta never helps eliminate scam accounts clearly trying to impersonate my husband. People have even given these scammers money thinking it was him! Friends with substantial followings have had similar issues, and no one helps. Most recently, I wished to further define my audience in REMOVEDads. When I did so, unbeknownst to me, it auto-checked a setting that included people outside of my desired age-range, causing an influx of unqualified leads to enter my funnel. I noticed the influx after a few days, and was able to pinpoint this checkbox. I asked REMOVEDsupport for a credit to my ad account since I did not consent to the addition (and there was no warning/notification that anything else was changed except for the changes I personally made). They have tossed me around to over 8 people, with REMOVEDminute wait times between each person, including a phone call which failed to resolve the issue. I am near certain they have training to just bounce a person with issues around until they get so frustrated they give up. I was simply asking for $50 to be credited to my ad account. So disappointed. Looking into other forms of advertising to get away from REMOVED. Not that they care at all. If you are looking to advertise for your business, start elsewhere to the best of your abilities. It is overly complicated and difficult to make simple edits, the system checks boxes you have no desire to check without your notification, and there will be zero help when you need it.

reviews.name: Andre P
reviews.text: People have been using my business assets to scam others. A simple Meta Verified badge can confer confidence to my clients, but I have been put on a Wait List inexplicably for 3 years. Multiple AI chats, a rare human chat, and even more rare human phone call did not yield anything whatsoever. So now we have an ongoing safety and liability issue that can be resolved by REMOVED, but apparently only God can intervene.

complaints.text: On Aug 26, 2026, my Meta business portfolio "Firewalker" (Business ID: REMOVEDwas restricted under REMOVED's Advertising Standards on Account Integrity, citing use of automation. I requested a review; on Aug 27, 2026, the restriction was upheld with no further appeal option available.I believe this is a false positive:The portfolio had zero activity history. No ads were ever created or run, no audiences uploaded, no money spent. It was restricted immediately after initial setup.All setup was performed manually by me in a standard web browser. No scripts, bots, browser automation, or third-party tools were used.Shortly before the restriction, I switched home internet providers to REMOVED. I have verified my new IP address against Spamhaus and REMOVEDTalos; it has no abuse or blocklist listings. REMOVED's own interface separately showed me a message that I was using "a device you don't usually use," suggesting the restriction was triggered by unfamiliar connection/device signals rather than actual automation.I am the sole owner of REMOVED, a registered Wisconsin company, and I am willing to complete business verification and identity verification to confirm REMOVEDpersonal Facebook account and personal ad account remain in good standing with no advertising issues.I am requesting a manual human review of the restriction on Business ID REMOVEDand its removal, or a clear path to verify my business and identity so it can be lifted.

I purchased my Meta REMOVEDglasses in April 2026. On August 27, 2026, I attempted to record a video and received a message stating that my camera had been REMOVEDglasses have never been altered or tampered with in any way. The LED and camera lenses are both completely intact. I have read numerous reports online from other customers experiencing the same issue, including customers who also state that they never modified their glasses.I understand REMOVEDmay have implemented camera-disabling measures to prevent users from tampering with or covering the recording LED. However, customers who have not altered their glasses should not have their camera functionality disabled. This has made a major feature of the product unusable through no fault of my own.I purchased these glasses expecting all advertised features to remain functional. Since REMOVEDhas disabled my camera despite there being no modification or damage to my glasses, I am requesting a full refund of the purchase price.

I am a paid REMOVEDVerified subscriber. My Facebook Marketplace access was restricted after Facebook's automated systems flagged my account for "unusual activity." Facebook requested that I verify my identity by submitting government-issued identification. I complied, and the identification matches the name and identity on my Facebook account. Immediately following the identity-verification process, my Marketplace access was permanently disabled. I contacted REMOVEDthrough the human support service provided with my paid REMOVEDsubscription. REMOVEDrepresentatives have informed me that they have no evidence that I violated Marketplace policies or Community Standards. I was further informed that the restriction was generated by REMOVED's automated/AI systems and that REMOVED's human support representatives cannot override the automated decision.I have requested human review and escalation, but REMOVEDhas been unable or unwilling to provide a meaningful review of the automated determination. I am requesting assistance obtaining an actual human review of the underly account-integrity determination and restoration of Marketplace access if REMOVEDcannot identify a policy violation supporting the restriction.

This complaint concerns REMOVEDcontinuing denial of my access to Facebook Marketplace. Although the restriction began in August 2023, it remains active today. During the past year, REMOVEDhas continued to block my Marketplace access, continued to display the restriction on my personal Facebook account, and recently failed to resolve it after directing me through a new verification and review process.The original restriction occurred after I listed legitimate rental properties for lease. Facebook alleged that my profile or activity may have deceived people to take their money, property or personal information.This allegation is false. The rental properties were legitimate, and I had legal authority to offer them for lease. I did not advertise nonexistent properties, impersonate another owner, or attempt to obtain anyones money, property, or personal information through deception.I appealed several times, but Facebook denied the appeals without identifying the specific listing, statement, transaction, complaint, or evidence supporting its accusation. Facebook later stated that the restriction was not eligible for further review.This is not merely a complaint about a decision made in 2023. REMOVEDis continuing to enforce the restriction today. Every time I attempt to access Marketplace, REMOVEDcontinues to deny access. The restriction has therefore caused an ongoing loss of access during the past year and remains unresolved.More recently, I purchased REMOVEDVerified and contacted its support service. REMOVEDinstructed me to complete identity verification and submit a contact form to Facebook management. I completed both steps and was told that the matter would be reviewed and resolved within a few days. Approximately one month has passed, but REMOVEDhas provided no decision, explanation, or follow-up, and it continues to block my Marketplace access.I am asking REMOVEDto stop maintaining an unsupported restriction or provide a fair, evidence-based review.

On August 24, 2026, an unauthorized person accessed my Facebook account from REMOVEDwhile I was asleep, despite two-factor authentication being enabled. Metas own security email identified the unauthorized Hong Kong login.The attacker added unauthorized contact information. I was able to remove some of it, but Facebook then locked and disabled my account. I completed Metas required video-selfie verification twice. Shortly afterward, REMOVEDpermanently disabled the account and stated that no further review was available. The private This wasnt me security link now returns an error, and the standard hacked-account process has temporarily blocked me from trying again.This has also removed my access to legitimate business assets that I owned and operated, including REMOVED, smover, alldays, and the advertising account named withPhilipJohnson. I have historical Facebook advertising receipts, payment records, Page identifiers, business-formation documents, and the original Meta security emails establishing my ownership and the unauthorized intrusion.This is not a disagreement with a content-moderation decision. It is an account-security failure followed by an automated disabling decision against the victim of the intrusion.Requested resolution:1. Escalate the matter to a human account-security specialist.2. Review the REMOVEDunauthorized-login evidence and the timing of the subsequent suspension.3. Restore access to my legitimate Facebook profile and associated business assets.4. Remove any remaining unauthorized administrators, email addresses, telephone numbers, sessions, or permissions.5. Confirm that my advertising account and stored payment information have been secured.6. Provide a working recovery channel rather than redirecting me to unavailable or broken automated forms.

I am filing this complaint against REMOVEDregarding improper copyright/REMOVEDclaims affecting my Instagram account. I hold registered trademark and copyright IP for my character. I have submitted proper counter-notifications citing official registrations, but my business operations have been unfairly impacted. I request immediate manual review, restoration of my account, and resolution regarding financial damages caused to my brand assets.

reviews.name: Randall Q
reviews.text: Virginia Mason Franciscan Health system is a prime example of what happens when healthcare becomes a profit-driven industry devoid of compassion. As a registered nurse myself, it's appalling to witness such blatant disregard for patients' well-being and financial stability. Let's start with the ludicrous assertion that they accept your insurance, which supposedly is in-network, only to later stick you with a bill that amounts to a mere fraction of what they should be receiving. This deceptive practice is not only unethical but also undermines the trust patients place in their healthcare providers. Furthermore, the exorbitant charges for basic procedures like an EKG are nothing short of robbery. Paying an EKG tech a paltry $27 per hour while charging patients a whopping $310 for a 10-minute procedure is not just unjustifiable but downright exploitative. It's clear where their priorities lie maximizing profits at the expense of patients' financial well-being. And let's not forget about the cardiologist who swoops in for a mere 5 minutes, dispenses generic advice like "cut down on coffee," and then has the audacity to bill a staggering $428. This egregious overcharging is not only a slap in the face to patients but also a reflection of the broken healthcare system that prioritizes profits over patient care. What's even more despicable is that they're pulling these stunts on their own network of healthcare professionals, who dedicate their lives to caring for others. It's a betrayal of trust and a REMOVEDreminder of how deeply entrenched corruption has become within the healthcare industry. In conclusion, Virginia Mason Franciscan Health Clinics and Hospital system exemplifies everything that's wrong with our healthcare system today greed, deception, and a blatant disregard for patients' well-being. It's time for accountability and reform to ensure that healthcare remains a fundamental right, not a privilege reserved for the wealthy and well-connected.

complaints.text: A medical device was placed to treat my diagnosed condition. The diagnosis is not in dispute. The treatment was medically necessary and in my best interest in the opinion of the final treating doctor. I was not told the device was not covered by insurance prior to the treatment. Therefore, I had the expectation that the doctor's billing service would code an insurance claim correctly and supply the necessary documentation to support the claim. In this case the claim for the device was specifically denied and Virginia Mason Franciscan Health (VMFH) tried to bill me $2570. First they claimed the device is never covered. That is patently not true. Both my insurance and the REMOVEDinsurance Commissioner( SHIBA) state the device is covered for treatment of my condition if properly coded and documented. Per SHIBA reading the denial, the claim was coded wrong, not completed correctly in box 19, & lacking all required supporting documentation. REMOVEDInsurance Commissioner provided the REMOVEDrules and instructions to properly file the claim. Then REMOVEDclaimed I should have known my insurance and it was not covered. AGAIN, patently not true. They have offered a discount price of $1156.50. and said that I need to file an appeal with the insurances. UNACCEPTABLE! If claimed correctly ins should pay 100% & at NO cost to me. REMOVEDis alleging they have refiled the claim, appealed the claim and it is rejected, multiple times. According to my insurance the only claim on file is the original incorrect coded and undocumented claim and the only appeal is the one I filed. I have been asking for copies of the claims REMOVEDsupposedly filed & they are not responding at all. I am asking REMOVEDto assume the responsibility for correctly coding and documenting the choice of their specialist doctor and to cease billing me. It was their ignorance and mistake to begin with and now they are trying to make it my problem. It is their mistake to correct. I have not paid the billed amount.

REMOVED, Virginia Mason Franciscan Health Corporate Responsibility Officer, REMOVED

complaints.text: St. Joseph (VMFH) is billing us $225.99 for each of three lactation visits ($677.97 total) because they will not correct the code to reflect a lactation visit and not an outpatient visit for our baby. After numerous outreach attempts, we are awaiting this to finally be resolved.
complaints.businessResponse: Thank you for contacting us regarding these concerns.  We are in the process of adjusting the involved accounts as necessitated with the insurance company that we have on record.  We are also in direct contact with the reporter to keep them apprised of any responsibility on their part as the claims for services rendered at our facility are appropriately adjudicated.  Feel free to contact me if I can provide any additional information or details.  Thanks - REMOVED, Virginia Mason Franciscan Health Corporate Responsibility Officer REMOVED

reviews.name: Karen P
reviews.text:
I've been an Eagle Tire customer since 2020 and have only used the REMOVEDlocation up until 11/6/2025, when I needed work done and used the closest branch in REMOVED. Having done business with them for so long I thought I'd get great support and service, but my recent experience was the polar opposite of what I have come to expect. On the morning of 11/6/25 I was in an accident that damaged the left rear lateral arm, trailing arm, knuckle, precisions suspension control arm, and spindle nut. I had the car towed to Eagle Tire and asked them to diagnose the issue that caused the accident. They said yes, quoted $170 to do the diagnosis and started the review on the morning of 11/7/25. The quote for the work to be done was $2,220.27 (less the $59.40 convenience fee as I wasn't using a credit card). I opened a claim with REMOVEDand because of the holiday and the delays with vacations at Eagle Tire, on 11/21/25 Eagle Tire agreed to the price set by American Family of $1,949.85. On that day I let REMOVEDknow that if that price wasn't agreeable, I'd need to know as any additional costs beyond the $1,949.85 would be payable by me. He let me know they'd agree to that price and that they'd be able to get the car back to me by 11/24. On 11/24 I called and was told parts they ordered didn't come in. 11/25 I called to pick up the car and I was quoted $2800 over the phone. REMOVEDlater called and told me they needed additional parts and completed the repair and now the costs were $2,511.45. RCW 45.76.025 states that costs exceeding 10% of the original quote require the owner's permission to proceed & the car can't be held as collateral for payment. I was not notified of the cost increase. 11/25 REMOVEDfiled a supplemental claim & refused to release my car to me. 12/1 an agreed upon increase was reached and my car was released to pick up, which I did on 12/4. This company violates WA state law, was rude to me during the process, & are dishonest. Take your car elsewhere

complaints.text: I took my 2022 REMOVEDOutlander in for an oil change on 02/02/26. I normally service my vehicle at the REMOVEDdealership, but due to distance I chose Jiffy Lube, believing it was a reasonable alternative.After the service, everything initially appeared fine and I drove home without issue. However, the following day at approximately 3 PM, my vehicle suddenly shut off while I was driving in the street with my children inside. The oil warning light had come on. I immediately contacted Jiffy Lube. After multiple attempts to restart the vehicle, it completely lost power and would not start.The store manager came to inspect the vehicle but did not provide any diagnosis. Instead, I was given contact numbers for towing companies. Using my insurance, I had the vehicle towed to the Jiffy Lube location on REMOVED. I was informed that a master technician would inspect the vehicle the next morning.The next day, I received a call stating that the battery was dead, that it had been charged, and that the vehicle was ready for pickup. I retrieved the vehicle, but within a few days the same problem occurred. While driving on I-94 in the express lane, the vehicle shut off again, nearly causing an accident.I then had the vehicle towed to a REMOVEDdealership. After inspection, their technicians asked when the last oil change had been performed. I explained it had been done about a week prior at Jiffy Lube. I was then informed that the engine had been overfilled with oil, which can cause serious mechanical failure.I have attempted to resolve this matter directly with Jiffy Lube management and have been extremely patient. Unfortunately, no meaningful initiative or accountability has been taken. Due to safety concerns for myself and my children, I no longer felt comfortable driving the vehicle and was forced to obtain a replacement.This situation created a dangerous safety risk and significant financial hardship.
