It seems the problem is they have administrative problems and has not taken this matter seriously. However, this money is for a 92 year old elderly person who is on a fixed income social security and desperately needs this money. It may not be important to a multi-billion dollar company like H&R Block, but it is very important to her. I have attached all of the correspondence and I am hoping you can see to it that they either give her the refund, or provide a legal reason why they have not given her the refund.
complaints.businessResponse:

That said, in the interest of client care and as a one-time courtesy, we have agreed to honor the client’s requested resolution. complaints.text:
In 2022, my husband and I filed tax returns with Indianapolis H&R Block Advisors. Despite informing, discussing, and providing ALL documentation of an SSA lump sum payment, our advisor failed to include the payment on our IRS and State returns. When the returns were filed, we received a $2000 IRS refund. Surprised, I asked the H&R Block advisor how a refund was possible since I received a lump sum. Shocked, she stated she forgot to include it and would have to file an amendment. She told us, however, not to worry because we were eligible to file an H&R Block “Peace of Mind” claim. I've attached emails regarding the claim and H&R Block's continued admissions of the error.

Despite overwhelming written evidence, the claim was denied. After the turmoil and financial strain of paying IRS late fees and penalties, I later received an INDOR notice that taxed the lump sum reported in the IRS Amendment. I had to protest the taxation myself, fill out paperwork, and comb through documents to submit the protest to the Indiana Department of Revenue. The protest was approved. However, due to the absence of a State amendment, INDOR sent a notice this month indicating that the EITC calculation omitted the lump sum amount. Now, I must pay the overpaid EITC credit, accumulated interest, and penalties from 2022.

Attached emails show that I specifically asked the H&R Block advisor if an Indiana Tax return needed to be filed. Her written response in the emails stated that an Indiana State amendment did not need to be filed. On August 12, 2025, I contacted the local H&R Block office. One of the advisors had the audacity to ask me if I had purposely told the 2022 advisor not to file an Indiana Amendment. H&R Block failed a loyal customer and does not care about making things right. We should not have been responsible for the 2022 mistake, and should not have to pay the INDOR charges of the July 28, 2025 notice when we were told an Indiana State Amendment did not need to be filed.

reviews.text: Absolutely terrible experience. I was told the process would take about 20 days. Since then, I have called and emailed over and over, spoken with multiple representatives, and received repeated promises that someone would contact me by the end of the day. Nobody calls back. Nobody gives a real answer. The claim just stays "under review."What makes me angry is that Expedia is the one promoting and selling this insurance during checkout. They take your money while making the product sound like protection for your trip, but when you actually need help, you are pushed off to a third-party company and left to deal with this nightmare REMOVEDmy opinion, the way Expedia presents this travel protection is extremely misleading. If Expedia is going to profit from promoting Travel Guard, they should also take responsibility for the quality of the company and the service their customers receive.This has been one of the worst customer service experiences I have had. complaints.text: CONTRACT REMOVEDVehicle:2020 REMOVEDGLE 350 4MATIC Contract Purchase Date:May 17, 2026 Odometer at Contract Purchase:67,093 miles Date Symptoms First Appeared / Vehicle Presented for Repair:August 15, 2026 Odometer at Reported Failure:67,347 miles Date Diagnostic Testing Performed:August 18, 2026 I purchased an extended auto warranty on May 17, 2026. The contract states: The Contract establishes a specific two-part test for a Pre-existing Condition.The Contract defines a Pre-existing Condition as:Any damage, failure, or Breakdown that existed prior to the Contract Purchase Date which would have been obvious and apparent if that component was inspected at the time of Contract purchase.Accordingly, May 17, 2026 the Contract Purchase Date is the relevant date for purposes of this exclusion.Under the plain language of the Contract, it is not enough to establish that a leak may have developed gradually or that an inspector believes it did not happen overnight.For the Pre-existing Condition exclusion to apply, there must be evidence establishingboth:that the specific damage, failure, or Breakdown existedprior to May 17, 2026; and that the condition would have beenobvious and apparent upon inspection of the component on May 17, 2026. The denial communicated to me does not establish either requirement.The Contract distinguishes gradual deterioration from a contractual Breakdown. The Contract separately defines Breakdown/Mechanical Breakdown in terms of a Covered Part becoming unable to perform the function for which it was designed because of a qualifying defect. The Contract also expressly recognizes that deterioration and reduction in performance can occur before a contractual Breakdown occurs, including by providing that gradual wear or reduction in performance becomes a Breakdown when the applicable wear exceeds the manufacturer's published tolerance.

complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for the opportunity to respond to REMOVEDcomplaint, BBB case # REMOVED. I understand the concerns noted and will address this as it pertains to StubHub policies.
It may help to explain that StubHub is a secondary ticket marketplace which enables fans to buy and sell tickets to sports, concert, theater, and other live entertainment events. We do not own any of the tickets listed on our site. When buyers place an order for tickets,they are purchasing from a third-party seller who sets their own prices for the tickets listed.

By using our website, buyers and sellers agree to the terms of our User Agreement. As part of our User Agreement, our FanProtect Guarantee for buyers notes, You will get your tickets in time for the event. Your tickets will be valid for entry. Your tickets will be the same as or comparable to those you ordered. If any of these things do not occur and you comply with applicable policies and timelines, we will find you comparable or better tickets to the event, or offer you a refund of what you paid for your purchase or credit of the same amount for use on a future purchase. complaints.text: Complaint against Allstar Lending, LLC I am filing this complaint due to repeated unwanted solicitations from Allstar Lending, LLC despite multiple requests to be removed from their mailing list.Over the course of several weeks/months, I have contacted this company at least 10 times requesting that my name and address be removed from their marketing and mailing database. These requests have been ignored, and I continue to receive unsolicited junk mail.This ongoing behavior demonstrates a clear disregard for consumer privacy and opt-out rights. At this point, the repeated contact is no longer just an inconvenienceit is intrusive and borders on harassment.I am requesting that Allstar Lending, LLC:Immediately remove my information from all marketing and mailing lists;Confirm in writing that my information has been permanently deleted;Cease all future contact.If this issue is not resolved promptly, I will consider pursuing additional complaints with relevant regulatory authorities.I expect this matter to be taken seriously and resolved without further delay.
complaints.businessResponse:
Allstar Lending, LLC acknowledges receipt of your complaint and has conducted a review of the information provided.
At this time, we have no record of prior opt-out or removal requests associated with your name and address in our systems. Notwithstanding, upon receipt of this complaint, we have taken immediate steps to ensure your preferences are honored.

Specifically, we have:

Removed your information from our internal marketing and mailing databases
Placed your information on our internal suppression list
Notified any applicable third-party vendors to cease further mailings

To the extent the mailings you received were part of prescreened credit offers, such communications are governed by the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), which permits such offers under defined conditions and provides consumers the right to opt out of future solicitations. Additionally, our marketing practices are designed to align with applicable federal and state regulations, including the CAN-SPAM Act, where applicable.
Please note that you may continue to receive materials that were already in production or in transit prior to the implementation of your opt-out. No new marketing communications will be initiated.
Allstar Lending, LLC maintains policies and procedures intended to comply with applicable consumer protection and privacy laws, including processes to honor opt-out requests when received. We will continue to review and, where appropriate, enhance these processes.
If you believe you previously submitted opt-out requests or if you continue to receive communications beyond 30 days, please contact us directly at [contact information] so we may investigate further.
Sincerely,

Title: Left Stranded Abroad - A Frustrating and Unfair Experience I had a terrible experience with CheapTickets (a brand under Expedia). I purchased a ticket that turned out to be invalid, leaving me stranded in a foreign country with no way home. Despite spending countless hours on the phone trying to reach customer service and higher management, I was consistently stonewalled. They refused to provide a direct contact, email, or any way to escalate the issue. After following their user agreement, which required arbitration, I filed a formal case and located their registered agent and legal department. However, the company never responded to the arbitration or paid the required fees - essentially stalling the process they themselves demanded. I believe they use the CheapTickets brand as a shield to deflect responsibility from REMOVED. Their structure makes it nearly impossible for the average consumer to get support or accountability. I feel misled, mistreated, and defrauded. Not only did they fail to resolve my issue, they gave me false hope while running out the clock. I live in REMOVEDand believe my rights under California consumer law were violated. This company's policies are not only unfair they seem intentionally designed to prevent consumers from getting help or justice. I'm pursuing further action and want to warn others before they make the same mistake.

I pointed out to her that she had no problem cancelling the appointment when I arrived on 7/27/2027, after 5 reminders/confirmations and no call or voicemail cancellations. Though I showed her my phone log, she was insistent she called, and that if she called, she would have left a message. I purchased the hearing aids 2.5 years ago from Robert Obrien/Connect Hearing. Big raspberry for really poor communication and unwilling to take ANY responsibility. I've confirmed for 8/3/2026 at 9 am, and we'll see what happens.

complaints.text: The cited office says it will call when the reconfigured earpiece(s) is delivered. But they do not. When I am able to contact them, after an extensive delay, the response is Oh REMOVEDjust delivered them. That is followed by a lame excuse for the delay. I have experienced this methodology many times in modified formats. The latest cShell correction remains difficult to insert into my left ear canal, it is too large and its tubing is too short. Its fit is uncomfortable at first, and painful after 4 to 6 hours of use.Once installed, movement of my jaw causes a discernable chafing/popping sound, and when eating it generates an overbearing amplified sound similar to a cow chewing REMOVEDthe first instance I have two choices: Clinch my teeth or keep my mouth open to stop the incessant chafing. And in the second, I have to stop eating to understand what is being said or I must press up at the base of my ear to stop the bovine chewing to join the conversation.Each iteration to adapt the ill-fitting cShell made it worse. After receiving the third iteration of the earpiece on Friday, I immediately called the subject AudioNova office on the following Monday. There was no answer. So, I recorded my request for an appointment, which was not fulfilled. About 10 days later, after multiple attempts, I was able to speak to the receptionist and was told that the audiologist was not available, but she would have him call me when he was available the following day. That also never occurred. Subsequently, every call thereafter has not been answered. It did not matter whether I called first thing in the morning, midday or in the afternoon, no one answers. My calls are being filtered. How and where can I get relief? AudioNova lacks access to regional customer service or means of reaching out to a regional manager.
complaints.businessResponse:
Dear Better Business Bureau and REMOVED,

Thank you for bringing this matter to our attention. At AudioNova, we take all patient feedback seriously and strive to provide both exceptional clinical care and reliable, open communication. We welcome the opportunity to provide an update on this matter,as our clinic team met directly with Mr. REMOVEDon 07/28/26 to address and resolve his concerns.

Regarding the cShell Fit and Clinical Care:
During the appointment, our clinic team listened thoroughly to Mr. REMOVEDspecific concerns regarding the comfort and performance of the earpiece. The mold was taken to our lab immediately for in-office physical adjustments. We are pleased to report that Mr. REMOVEDseemed satisfied with these modifications and found the fit improved before leaving the clinic. To ensure a permanent solution,we have also officially ordered a brand-new manufacturer remake of the mold with these precise structural corrections implemented.

Regarding Communication and Accessibility:
We want to ensure that Mr. REMOVEDalways has seamless, reliable access to our team moving forward. To resolve any potential phone or connection issues, our hearing care provider supplied Mr. REMOVEDwith their personal cell phone number. The patient has been instructed to call the provider directly if he ever experiences difficulty reaching the clinic or needs immediate assistance.

Proposed Resolution:
We believe the actions taken on 07/28/26 have addressed both the immediate fit of the device and the communication concerns. We will continue to track the arrival of the new remake closely and will coordinate directly with Mr. REMOVEDfor his fitting. We appreciate his patience and collaboration as we work to finalize this solution.

Sincerely,
AudioNova REMOVEDTeam

complaints.text: 6/4/26 I am filing this complaint regarding Audionova in REMOVED, REMOVED, after being denied access to my own recent audiogram results unless I paid a $40 fee. I am currently unemployed and explained my financial situation to the staff, but I was still told that I would need to pay in order to receive a copy of my medical records.An audiogram is part of my personal health information, and I requested it so I could pursue further evaluation and explore hearing-related assistance programs. Instead of providing reasonable access to my records, Audionova imposed a fee that creates a barrier to my ability to manage my own healthcare. I was not informed of this charge at the time of my appointment, nor was I given any documentation stating that obtaining my results would require an additional payment.I believe this practice is unfair, especially for patients experiencing financial hardship. I am simply asking for a copy of my own audiograminformation that directly concerns my health and that I should be able to access without excessive or unexpected fees. I am requesting the BBBs assistance in resolving this matter and ensuring that I receive my audiogram results without being charged $40.
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for bringing this matter to our attention. Our goal is always to ensure patients have seamless access to their hearing healthcare information and receive excellent service.
After reviewing the case, we believe a misunderstanding occurred, as our standard policy is to provide patients with copies of their records upon request. We have addressed this with our clinic staff to ensure clearer communication moving forward.

To resolve this concern immediately, we are providing a copy of the audiogram. We sincerely apologize for any frustration this situation caused and appreciate the opportunity to correct it.

complaints.text: I have a pair of hearing aids which I purchased from a different provider at Connect Hearing on REMOVEDin REMOVED, REMOVEDbefore AudioNova took over. I have a service contract I had purchased from Connect Hearing. So, my hearing aids suddenly stopped amplifying; took them in to AudioNova and REMOVEDreplaced the wires to the receivers. Fast forward, went out again, and again had REMOVEDreplace. Fast forward, realized that since about the time the wires were replaced the sound on my hearing aids sees off - less clarity, distortion, etc. I went in for an appointment to discuss, REMOVEDdid an updated hearing test and did some programming adjustments. Now, the issues persist. Now, as I was double checking my receiver type before buying a new pack of domes, I noticed they said 2 P. That means the receivers REMOVEDplaced on my hearing aids when he replaced the wires are 2 prong. These specific hearing aids, the Audeo L90, are not supposed to have below a 3 prong. With a 2 prong; sound distortion and other amplifying problems are known to happen. The 2 prong arent actually even supposed to fit these hearing aids. Extremely disappointed as I paid good money for the hearing aids I have due to the improved amplification and clarity, yet here I am having repairs done with parts that are not equivalent to what I originally had, and which are known to be incompatible. Id love to be able to be refunded for the remainder of the service contract so I can just go elsewhere. And/or to be connected to a provider more competent and capable of properly fixing my hearing aids.

complaints.text: On 10/13/25 I purchased hearing aids from AudioNova and returned them on 11/12/25. There was a guaranteed refund if returned within 45 days. They were returned in 29 days. As of today12/14/25 I have neither seen the check nor heard from them.
complaints.businessResponse: Refund check was issued and sent on 12/12/2025.

complaints.text: I got a flyer in the mail from audio nova. It had a coupon for a 75-dollar gift card if you had a hearing evaluation. So, I had a hearing evaluation 8-12-2025 and even tried hearing aids returning them 8-18-2025. I asked at the check in about the gift card and was told all the information had been entered. So, I waited a bit longer and then sent an email to REMOVEDthe hearing instrument specialist that did my test. I indicated to her the non-response to my first email and also indicated I did not receive a gift card nor any communications from audio nova. I also indicated I would file a complaint if I did not hear back. Well, have not heard a thing. I went there in good faith, got tested and even tried the hearing aids. The business has not been honorable in what the offer promised. Its only 75 dollars Im out but the business principle is downright fraudulent. Please help me out. Thank you.
complaints.businessResponse: We reached out to Mr. REMOVEDearlier today, verified his mailing address and will be sending the $75 Gift Card to his home address.

complaints.text: Purchased hearing aids for $3500 on a Care Credit (REMOVED) account with interest-free terms (number of months not established). I have a dispute entered with Synchrony and auto payments are on hold until the issue is resolved/or denied by them. Thank you.

We are in contact with the customer regarding the financing of her purchase and are currently coordinating a resolution with the financing company, REMOVEDregarding the interest credits. We hope to have a resolution very soon, waiting on a callback from their representative.

Your AudioNova Team.

complaints.text: I left my hearing aids with AudioNova store in REMOVED, REMOVEDon 6 March 2025 to have fixed since the left hearing aid wasn't holding a charge. The dispenser was to send them to be fixed. After numerous phone calls, I was told they didn't know where they were. I was given 2 pair of trial aids at different times to use in the interim, which both are no longer working since they only last 45 days. I reached REMOVEDon an appointment line, which in turn forwarded my problem to her supervisor, REMOVED. (25 Aug 25) He called the Dispenser at the REMOVEDstore & she told him she had ordered me a replacement pair. 9 Sep 25, the Dispenser told me mine was coming by REMOVEDthat day. She called and said they didn't come, they would be here the next day. I've heard nothing & they won't answer the phone. Went by the office twice last week and there was a closed sign on the door. I need my hearing aids. I've been with them for years & invested a lot of money. They were under warranty in March, but warranty runs out 17 Sep 25. My insurance has changed policy. Instead of a partial payment every 3 yrs, it's now every 5 years. If I have to buy another pair now, I will have to pay full price. Please help me get another pair of hearing aids as I need them. Thanks for your time and understanding.
complaints.businessResponse: We are aware of the patient's issue - a repair that was sent back to the manufacturer, Phonak.  We are monitoring the situation daily for the status and will reach out to the patient as soon as we hear back from Phonak.  In the meantime, a loaner pair of hearing aids has been given to the patient in the interim. Warm Regards.

complaints.text: In April of this year, I went to AudioNova/connect hearing and purchased hearing aids. At the time the girl said she would file a claim with my insurance company but that I needed to pay $2275.50 because that was what they estimated my portion to be. I paid the $2275.50 to them that day when I received my hearing aids. Soon after I got the explanation of benefits from my insurance company and after the agreed upon PPO adjustment my insurance company paid $3846.50 which left the remaining $427.50 the only amount, I was to pay. I overpaid them by $1847.50. Since then, I have tried many times to get a hold of anyone at AudioNova/Connect Hearing to get my refund of my overpayment but to no availnow all my calls go to voicemail, and I dont get a call back. I really need assistance with this because Im a single retired woman and $1847.50 is a lot of money to me and way too much to be ripped off.
complaints.businessResponse:
Dear Ms. REMOVEDapologize for the delay as we are still working with your insurance to balance the account before we can evaluate and issue a refund. The notes from our insurance specialist show REMOVEDsending a benefit payment to REMOVED, REMOVED. We have contacted them multiple times requesting information to track down the payment. As of 9/10 we have still not received that benefit check from them and their portal status is that it is being reviewed we will be contacted.

Again, we apologize on behalf of your REMOVEDinsurance, but we are unable to bring to account current until that payment issue is resolved. In our experience, this can take several months.  We will continue to press them to resolve it and fast track your account once received.

Kindest Regards,

complaints.text: Transaction Date: [08/03/2026]Amount Paid to Business: $410.50 Business Commitment: To provide four safe, road-worthy tires (Continental ControlContact Sport SRS Plus).I purchased four tires from United Tires LLC for $410.50. Upon installation, the shop discovered that two of the tires were severely defective: one had a deep structural sidewall cut, and the second had a hole punctured completely through the sidewall, making it completely unable to hold air.This created an immediate emergency. The shop refused to put my original tire back on because it was showing wire, and they had no matching tire sizes in stock. Because United Tires shipped dangerous inventory, I was forced to have the cut sidewall tire mounted just to leave the shop, putting me in an active, life-threatening highway blowout risk.Shipping inventory with structural sidewall damage is a critical product safety failure. While CCO REMOVEDsent two replacement tires as well as a $70 refund for the second mounting fees, providing replacements does not undo the severe danger, distress, and inconvenience caused by delivering hazardous stock that endangered my safety on the road.I am seeking a partial order refund of $200.00 (roughly 50% of the purchase price). reviews.text: The Nines at Kierland Review (Apartments.com-ready)We chose The Nines for convenience and advertised 24/7 on-site security. After about a year, that security was removed and the property no longer felt well protected. Office and maintenance communication was poor. Calls rarely reached a live person, messages went to an automated system, and callbacks often never came. I frequently had to visit the office in person just to get a response. Repair issues were also a problem: backed-up sinks, dishwashers, and washers that flooded the unit. Work orders sometimes took days or weeks. We later learned many units were being used as vacation rentals. Management would not identify who was staying in those units and said those stays were handled by a third-party company. After a police incident in an upstairs vacation unit near ours, staff said they did not know who had been living there. That lack of accountability made the community feel unsafe. We renewed in March 2026, then decided to leave about a month later. Early termination required 60 days notice plus a two-month buyout, and management said the owners would not negotiate. After move-out, a manager said only blinds and a deep clean were needed ($125 and $95). Months later we were told we would get only $35 back, and that refund still had not arrived after four months. The resident portal also changed often and frequently did not work.We wanted basic safety, communication, timely repairs, and follow-through. We did not get that. Ask detailed questions about security, after-hours response, vacation rentals, and deposit/early-termination policies before signing.

I talked to several different spectrum REMOVEDresentatives and none of them could provide me with any details on the network, as I was not the customer, REMOVEDwas. So all I had to go off of was what the apartment was telling me orally and in writing about how this network would function. I am a competitive gamer and I from time to time work from home for the government handling PII and PHI for the REMOVEDso having a personal network that I control was a major point of interest for my decision on which apartment to choose. After I had already signed the lease, I quickly realized a lot of the information I'd been provided about this network was just false on its face. I was provided a wifi password for an access point to the residents wifi network shared by all residents on the complex. I was finally able to speak to a REMOVEDat REMOVEDwho could provide specifics and they said the complex has a 300mbs fiber line that goes to the main office and then is distributed by wifi access points and that there were no options for a personal network without buying another plan. I went to the apartment and told them I wanted to opt out and they denied it, while stating "they do not control the speed" which is absurd, clearly they picked the plan, which is spectrums lowest possible speed. I would simply like them to allow to me opt out, as im going to have to buy my own plan anyways and eat the 70 dollar fee.
complaints.businessResponse:
Hello,

I have spoken with the regional manager and can offer the following context.

"REMOVEDmoved into REMOVEDon July 18, 2026. The property has a bulk cable and internet agreement with REMOVED, which is charged at $35 for cable and $35 for internet each month. These charges are included in his signed lease.
After moving in, REMOVEDcontacted the team because the internet setup was not what he expected. He stated that he was told he would be able to set up his own personal network and later received different information from REMOVED. Because of this, he requested to opt out of the bulk internet service and have the charge removed.

The onsite team spoke with REMOVEDregarding his concerns, and the issue was also escalated to me. We explained that the internet is part of a community-wide bulk agreement with Spectrum and that we are unable to remove the charge for an individual resident.
We also explained that Spectrum manages the actual internet service, speeds, network, and technical support. He was directed to Spectrum to discuss his service concerns and any available upgrade options.

We are not able to allow him to opt out or remove the monthly charge. The cable and internet are part of the property's bulk agreement with Spectrum, and the $35 cable and $35 internet charges are included in his signed lease.
He can choose to purchase additional or upgraded internet service if Spectrum offers it, but the bulk charges would remain on his account."

Thank you.

complaints.text: I am disputing deductions taken from my $2,200 security deposit, as well as the failure to return my separate $350 pet deposit, after moving out of my apartment at Filament REMOVEDmanaged by Avenue5 Residential. On July 30, 2026, Filament notified me of deductions they intended to take from my deposit. However, the vendor proposals they later relied upon to justify those deductions were not obtained until July 31, 2026, raising concerns that the charges had already been determined before the estimates were even requested. I contacted the flooring company directly. They confirmed they never inspected my apartment and prepared only a phone proposal based solely on the square footage provided by Filament. I was charged for a full carpet replacement. I also contacted the painting vendor, who confirmed the apartment had not been inspected before the estimate was prepared. I was charged more than $900 for painting related primarily to nail holes, yet the estimate was not based on an inspection of my unit. Additionally, Filament charged me $25 for cleaning that I had completed, even though the photographs they provided appear to show those areas in clean condition. My pet deposit was also withheld without an explanation or documentation showing how it was applied. When I requested supporting documentation and proof that these repairs were completed and paid for, Filament stopped responding to my emails and failed to return my calls. I am requesting that Avenue5 Residential and Filament provide documentation supporting these deductions, including proof of completed work and payment, reevaluate deductions that were based on estimates prepared without inspections, refund my pet deposit, reverse unsupported cleaning charges, and return any portion of my security deposit that was improperly withheld. I have retained the move-out statement, vendor proposals, photographs, correspondence, and information obtained directly from the vendors supporting my concerns.
complaints.businessResponse:
Hello,

I have spoken with the Regional Manager and can provide the following context:

"The $350 pet charge was a non-refundable pet fee, not a refundable pet deposit. The non-refundable nature of this fee was disclosed during the application process and included in the REMOVED(REMOVED) lease documents executed by the resident. Because it was a fee rather than a security deposit, it was not applied toward move-out charges and was not eligible for refund.
Our onsite management team conducts the initial move-out inspection and documents the condition of the apartment after possession has been returned. Those findings are used to prepare the deposit accounting statement and determine the work needed to restore the apartment. Vendors are then scheduled to complete the identified work. Accordingly, vendor proposals may be dated after the initial inspection or accounting notice because the vendors are provided with the scope, measurements, photographs, and other information documented by management. The fact that a vendor did not independently inspect the apartment before preparing a proposal does not mean the assessed work was unsupported or determined without an inspection; the underlying inspection was completed by the onsite management team.
The carpet, painting, and cleaning charges were assessed based on the condition documented during the move-out inspection and the work determined to be necessary. The $25 cleaning charge was not a general assessment of the residents overall cleaning efforts, but related to conditions identified during the inspection. Similarly, the painting and flooring charges were based on the documented condition and required restoration work, not solely on the dates appearing on the subsequent vendor proposals.
We regret that the resident felt their requests did not receive a timely response. Avenue5 Residential and Filament REMOVEDtake these concerns seriously and are prepared to provide the available records supporting the final accounting,

complaints.text: I am a tenant at the Avenue5-managed property, Beacon View Apartments in REMOVED(Unit A 407). I pay a separate, monthly line-item fee for assigned parking space #REMOVED. For months, Avenue5 has allowed an oversized, mechanically inoperable, and unregistered white truck to be permanently stored in the adjacent spot. This vehicle's rear end extends dangerously into the active drive aisle. Combined with the vehicles parked behind me, my vehicle's turn radius has been completely eliminated. Every single day, I am forced to execute hazardous maneuvers that severely risk scraping my car against this immobilized truck's bumper just to use the amenity I pay for. Local on-site management refused to act, falsely claiming they "cannot do anything." I have since sent TWO formal corporate legal demands via REMOVEDCertified Mail (First notice: June 18, 2026; Second notice: July 20, 2026) informing Avenue5 Corporate Leadership of their full legal authority under Washington States Private Property Impound Law (RCW 46.55.070) to issue a 72-hour notice and tow this lease-violating vehicle. Avenue5 Corporate has completely ignored both certified letters, failed to respond, and continues to willfully ignore a severe property safety hazard. I have not initiated any court action, as I prefer to resolve this administratively if Avenue5 Corporate takes immediate corrective action through the BBB.
complaints.businessResponse:
Hi,

I have spoken with the property manager and can provide the following context.

"The resident has complained to the office several times about a truck parked next to her due to the size making it inconvenient to pull in and out of her space. After looking at the vehicle, it was parked within the lines and it was in a rented parking spot. However, the truck was not the associated vehicle with the space, so we posted a notice on it. The owner of the vehicle promptly responded to the office and informed us that his vehicle information was updated, and provided us the information for the vehicle. After informing REMOVEDthat the spot was rented and was properly parked in the lines, we offered her an alternative space that may be more convenient for her, but she did not respond to that offer.

We have tried multiple times to offer her a different parking space, but she has not taken that option.

The last time I spoke with her, I told her I would email her a list of available spaces and she agreed that she would look at it, but never responded. This was the last time I interacted with her.

In the meantime, we can conduct a property-wide parking audit and notice any and all vehicles that contain expired registrations, if applicable."

At this time, your resolution has been offered to you many times, but if you'd like to, please reach out to the property manager to coordinate an updated parking spot.

Thank you.

complaints.text: Early September the first crew of packers came. Unbeknownst to us, they were taking items already packed and repacking them in the Two men and a truck boxes, costing us hundreds of dollars unnecessary. While doing this, it turns out that often they would use a medium size box for one small item, once again costing us more money unnecessarily. The second crew didn't ask for a tip and I insisted on giving them one. I'd like a refund for the boxes.
complaints.businessResponse:
This customer was challenging to pack and move. I have plenty of documentation and pictures that will attest to this. We describe this type of customer as a hoarder. My crew had to remove trash at the request of the customer just to make room to do any packing. Once the packing started it took 3 days. Our crew was being slowed down by the customer being right in front of them asking the crew to reopen boxes to see what was inside and then the crew had to repack the boxes. Most of the boxes were unusable, unstable, open top, etc. so they couldn't be used to stack in the moving truck. At one point a manager was onsite to politely ask the customer to stay out of the way so we could perform services in a timely manner because the customer had stated they had to be off the premises by a certain date. First and foremost, we are professionals and every service and container (box) we provided was required to complete the packing and moving. One final point would be our customers have the authority to request as much or as little service as they want. We accomodate because we are a customer service based company. This customer could have requested us to stop service at any time and we would have done so. Their packing and moving was expensive due to everything that had to be done but from all my pictures, texts, documents, etc.... a refund is not justified.

complaints.text: The move involved prepackaged materials, yet both pickup and delivery each took up to eight hours. This was with two crews totaling 9 team members. Given the scope, this timeframe was excessive and not reflective of an efficient or professionally managed move. Delays were largely due to poor coordination and communication. Movers routinely took 3045 minutes between stops, and multiple calls to drivers went unanswered, leaving us without updates. Reports for arrival and departure logs records were kept by staff and each point of delivery. At times, instructions were ignored, further slowing progress. Workflow inefficiencies were consistent. Movers often carried only one box at a time rather than maximizing each trip. Time also appeared to be spent on personal activities, such as stopping for ice cream and phone activities without communication or formally clocking out for breaks. Particularly concerning was the lack of experience handling artwork and archival materials. After multiple booking calls with REMOVEDand REMOVED, we were assured experienced staff would manage these items, which was not the case. They did not have the proper gloves or sanitary protocol for handling art. We supplied, butcher paper, painting corners, styrofoam padding and bubble wrap for artwork. On-site staff demonstrated knowledge gaps, requiring our intervention, while others stood idle awaiting direction for notable amounts of time. The second crew appeared unfamiliar with proper techniques for packing and handling artwork, despite prior notice request for art handling. Overall, excessive time, inefficiency, and poor coordination resulted in what we believe was overcharging for subpar service that did not match what was promised. Main office defaulted to phone communication on their terms over written confirmation, which created gaps and limited accountability.
complaints.businessResponse: Good morning, our customer service team has already worked with the client. Despite the issues with how everything was moved there were zero damages or issues with the artwork... This claim has been closed to the customers satisfaction.

complaints.text: I am a 64 year old woman who lives alone. I moved on 5/31/25 from one apartment to another that was roughly 9 minutes away. When I ordered the moving service, we're required to list our items that are being moved, bookcases, couches, chairs, beds, etc. I HAD NOT LARGE APPLIANCES TO MOVE. Everything that wasn't furniture was in boxes. When the movers did their walk-through, the trouble started. The boxes held clothing, linen, books, music cds, small kitchen appliances. A time limitation was introduced-if we go over this time, you'll have to pay $200 extra dollars. Things were placed in the apartment without any sense of order though my boxes were labeled. Clothing and linen were in the front of the apartment. Everything else was plunked down blocking ample closets where boxes could have been stacked. A full-size futon frame was set blocking a completely empty closet and surrounded by a sea of boxes in the back family room. in another bedroom, the futon mattress was left in the center of the room (again) blocking another completely empty closet. All these were surrounded by a sea of boxes in the center of the floor. They claimed they couldn't get my sofa into the front of the apartment, so it was left standing in the hallway. The lead mover quipped that I get my nephews to move it in for me because they had run out of time. When i got help to move the futon and the mattress did I discover that a REMOVEDcomputer, an 2T hard drive and two Bose speakers were missing. It was as though they deliberately blocked those closets so that I would think those electronics were inside. They took down 2 bookshelves but didn't leave the shelf pins with me. It was only after I had someone help me untie the futon and the mattress that I noticed that nothing was in the closets. I expected to find the REMOVEDcomputer, hard drive and the speakers there. Because in the day after call I said that the move when okay, the company is now saying I should have mentioned the lost items then.
complaints.businessResponse:
This was a move for a customer in REMOVED, REMOVED  We are located in REMOVED. REMOVED, REMOVED, and do not service that area.

Our leadership wonders if this customer has moved again with another company and is confusing them with us? As noted, we have a phone recording of the customer letting us know everything went well with their move.

complaints.text: I worked with REMOVEDand REMOVEDto move on May 3. I spoke to REMOVEDon Saturday and REMOVEDon Wednesday, to which no resolution was reached and I was not provided the contact information for anyone else to speak to. REMOVEDtold me that he started the timer at 11:45 before they had finished PARKING. I paid a flat fee of $184 for the transportation cost. I was DOUBLE BILLED, to which I am seeking a reimbursement. After I showed them what I want to be moved, REMOVEDquoted me $1029 - the maximum amount he could bill me. At no point was I told that movers will automatically quote you the max cost. When I asked why I was being billed $1029, instead of answering my question REMOVEDsaid that he had already started the timer at 11:45 and that every minute we talk is running up the clock. When I ask again he STILL refused to answer and instead he talked about how there are a lot of variables like traffic. When I ask for the THIRD TIME I also ask if the service doesnt take as long as expected will I be reimbursed. REMOVEDsays yes you will be reimbursed in REMOVEDhours.The movers themselves were incredibly slow. I had everything disassembled, packed up (with bubble wrap and plastic wrap as necessary), and set up with plenty of space for them to move. I even started moving things closer to the door as there was more space.REMOVEDwas CONSTANTLY vaping by the truck. He was still vaping at the new apartment and during the signing/billing process.The movers finish moving everything back in to the new place at 1:29. REMOVEDpointed to the oven on the way out and said "Its 1:30 now, Im going to stop the clock at 1:45." Given that I was done signing by 1:40, I dont understand why the timer is being rounded to the time on the clock. I was not ALLOWED to insure myself. I told them twice that I wanted to pay the $25 but REMOVEDCROSSES IT OFF and says I dont need to pay for it.
complaints.businessResponse: Hi, I believe you have been explained in detail the charges and had any other questions or concerns answered by our customer care team. Please let us know if you have any further questions - as of now, according to our notes this concern is closed.

complaints.text: A lot of my furniture was damaged during the move. The driver persuaded me to take the insurance off and I was under the influence of muscle relaxants and pain meds. I believe some of the items were damaged before then. Also, whoever wrote the order up stated I had 60 items, when I fact I said 60 boxes. I was overcharged and they are trying to add money and give me a fake layout thing to give me $50.00 in return. I attached a screenshot of the email sent to me for reference. I have photos of the damages but unable to upload do to the size of the file.
complaints.businessResponse: Hi REMOVED, I am sorry to hear you are not satisfied with our services. I am confused though, it does appear that your claim (both damage and customer service) is closed and you have been refunded. Can you please let me know where the disconnect is? I do not see any need for further refund as our management team has taken everything into consideration.

reviews.name: Farhan K
reviews.text:
I recently purchased a 2023 Mercedes-Benz GLS from Exclusive Auto House, and the entire experience was absolutely outstanding from start to finish. The team was professional, transparent, and genuinely focused on making sure I was comfortable and satisfied at every step.
The vehicle was exactly as described—immaculate condition, well maintained, and priced fairly. There was no pressure, no hidden surprises, and no last-minute changes, which I truly appreciated. They took the time to answer all my questions, explained everything clearly, and made the buying process smooth and stress-free.
What really sets Exclusive Auto House apart is their honesty and customer service. You can tell they take pride in their inventory and value long-term customer relationships, not just quick sales.
If you’re looking for a high-quality luxury vehicle and a dealership you can trust, I highly recommend Exclusive Auto House. I couldn’t be happier with my GLS and will definitely be returning for future purchases.

complaints.text: On June 15, 2026, I purchased a 2018 REMOVEDQ5 from Exclusive AutoHaus for $16,500 cash after repeatedly being told it was in excellent condition. Before purchase, a dealer employee accompanied me to a nearby repair shop, I was not informed of any significant mechanical problems.Shortly afterward, an oil/service warning led me to an independent REMOVED-experienced shop. It found oil leakage and problems with the engine mounts, upper timing cover, and water pump. I paid $1,800 for repairs plus $189 for the oil/service. The mechanic also told me oil and coolant had mixed and the condition could recur. The battery then failed; I paid $104 for a jump-start and was told the installed battery dated from 2017 and needed replacement. I have incurred $2,093 within about 1.5 months despite barely driving the vehicle.There is also a serious mileage discrepancy. The sales/odometer documents state REMOVEDmiles, but the vehicle showed REMOVEDmiles when I took possession. I raised this BEFORE signing. I was told the owner's wife had been driving the vehicle, explaining the additional mileage, and correcting the paperwork would take time. I was encouraged to proceed anyway. I preserved photos/videos showing REMOVEDmiles.I was rushed through signing without adequate time to review the documents. After signing, the dealer kept them for over an hour despite my requests. I later found the Buyer's Guide had IMPLIED WARRANTIES ONLY checked with AS-IS handwritten on it, while the Bill of Sale's SOLD AS IS box appears unchecked.Had I known the vehicle's actual condition, I would not have purchased it. I request that the dealer accept return of the vehicle and refund my $16,500; alternatively, reimburse my documented $2,093 expenses and related qualifying expenses.
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for bringing your concerns to our attention. We take customer satisfaction seriously and would like to clarify our position regarding this matter.

The mechanical concerns and repair expenses described in your complaint were not brought to our attention until now, approximately two months after the vehicle was purchased. Had these concerns been brought to our attention when they first arose, we would have inspected the vehicle, evaluated the reported issues, and determined what assistance we could provide before repairs were completed at an outside facility. Unfortunately, we were not given that opportunity, and approximately two months have now passed since the purchase.

We have always made reasonable efforts to assist our customers when concerns are brought to us in a timely manner. However, we cannot be responsible for repairs that were completed elsewhere without first being given an opportunity to inspect the vehicle or address the concerns ourselves.

At this point, we are unable to accept the return of the vehicle, refund the purchase price, or reimburse the requested $2,093 in repair and related expenses. However, in the interest of good customer relations and resolving this matter amicably, Exclusive AutoHaus is willing to offer $300 as a customer-service goodwill gesture.

This offer is being made strictly as a gesture of goodwill and customer service and should not be interpreted as an admission of liability or responsibility for the information described in the complaint.

complaints.text: I purchased a 2016 REMOVEDCrosstrek on November 29, 2025 from Exclusive Autohaus in REMOVED, REMOVED. Within 24 hours, the exhaust detached and exhaust fumes and odor were entering the cabin while driving. complaints.businessResponse:

Exclusive AutoHaus addresses concerns in good faith and through proper procedures. We remain willing to complete our inspection and move forward accordingly once the vehicle is returned.

complaints.businessResponse:
On August 6, 2025, the customer purchased a 2017 REMOVEDwith $7,000 down and submitted documents for financing. During the lenders verification process, the utility bill provided was found to be altered. Because of this, the bank treated it as a customer trying to commit fraud, hence denied the loan and returned the deal.
Once we were informed by the lender of the fraudulent paperwork, we took the vehicle back and issued the customer a notice letter following our internal policies and procedures, as outlined in the conditions of the contract.
Despite our standard return policy being limited to 7 days, we offered the following two options as a good faith effort:
-Return the downpayment minus the fees and penalties along with the mileage usage of the vehicle based on our return policy especially considering the vehicle had been driven over REMOVEDmiles without valid financing.

- The option to obtain her own financing or a cosigner to complete the purchase only if it gets approved with all the accurate and true paperwork.


The customer has instead demanded the full $7,000 back. Given the banks determination of attempt to fraud and our policies, we cannot comply with that demand. We remain willing to resolve the matter under the options already provided.

complaints.text: On the date of 02/14/2025 i started to finance a car with Exclusive Autohaus . I Paid an amount of 1500 down which included $500 zelle payment . I was told the car was up to date, i also test drove the car and it had a tire sensor on. The seller proceeded to tell me that the sensor was caused because of cold weather. Turns out the rim was cracked and i had to fix the problem out of pocket with no issues. At the time of the purchase of my car they sold me a third party warranty for 12 months or REMOVEDmiles that would cover the car if broke down. Less than 6 months of having the vehicle it broke down. I called Exclusive Autohaus and they told me to take it to REMOVEDdealership to have a diagnostic on my car and i found out my car was sold to me pre- modified and with out a catalytic converters. I also found out that the warranty they sold me would not cover modified cars. I called Exclusive Autohaus to try and resolve the issue and they told me that they are not willing to help or figure out a solution to the problem which was very un professional of them. I have called them multiple times to try and come to an agreement but they are not willing to take responsibility for selling a car that is modified and a warranty that does not cover the repairs which is fraud in the state of REMOVED. I will like to take further action if decided to not resolve this situation or come to an agreement.
complaints.businessResponse:
We are responding to the customers complaint regarding their February 14, 2025 vehicle purchase.
At the time of sale, the vehicle had no warning lights present. A few days later, the customer returned and stated the tire pressure light was on. While we are not a tire shop, we still went out of our way to assist. We took the vehicle to a third-party tire shop at our own expense, and they resealed the tire.
A few days later, the customer stated the tire was leaking again. We offered to take it back to the same shop (since the work had already been paid for and was under their service), but the customer chose instead to take it elsewhere. They later stated that the rim had been repaired, which suggests the wheel was damaged after the third partys initial repair, as the rim issue was not present when the vehicle left the shop after the reseal.
The customer has now raised additional concerns about catalytic converters and other modifications, more than six months after the sale. We have no knowledge of any such modifications at the time of sale, and the vehicle was sold in the condition as presented and functioning properly. These claims raise the possibility that changes were made to the vehicle after purchase, and we cannot be held responsible for modifications or alterations performed outside our dealership.
Regarding the extended warranty, this was an additional, optional purchase made by the customer at the time of sale. We do not include extended warranties in the purchase price or contract unless specifically chosen and paid for by the customer. The warranty terms and exclusions were explained in detail at delivery, and the customer was provided with copies of the coverage documents at that time.
As with all pre-owned vehicles, ongoing maintenance is the responsibility of the owner. We cannot speak to how the vehicle has been driven or maintained during the six months since purchase. Throughout this process, we have acted in good faith, addressed concerns promptly

complaints.text: Date of transaction : 11/14 2015 Chevrolet Silverado - $24,000 I bought this truck on 11/14 with 15 days/500 mile warranty. I had the truck for the first week then started to experience issues. Ticking noises in the engine bay, oil leaking under the body, muffler sounding louder than normal. I then set an appointment (11/25) to get it checked out by a certified mechanic. They expressed to me the problems and then I got a second opinion, same results. With the holidays coming up in that week is was tough to get the answer in a reasonable time frame. The 15 day period ending 11/29 but the truck has been in both shops since the initial appointment on the 25th. I attempted to call the company (Exclusive Autohaus) on 12/2 explaining to them the circumstances I am dealing with. They informed me that I am over my 15 day warranty and they are not obligated to do anything for me. I tried getting in contact with some lawyers to guide me in the right path to solve this issue.
complaints.businessResponse:
In response to the complaint regarding the 2015 Chevrolet Silverado purchased on 11/14, we would like to clarify that the vehicle was sold with an implied warranty, which is limited to a 15-day or 500-mile period, whichever occurs first. This warranty period includes all daysweekdays, weekends, and holidays.

According to the terms of the warranty, the customer was required to notify us of any issues within the 15-day or 500-mile time frame. The customer did not notify us of any concerns after their initial visit to the first REMOVEDshop on 11/25. Given that the customer was already in communication with a REMOVED, it would have been the appropriate time to notify us of the issues under warranty. Instead, the customer chose to get a second opinion before reaching out to us.

As the concerns were raised after the expiration of the warranty period, we are unfortunately unable to honor the warranty at this time. We understand the customers frustration, but we are bound by the agreed-upon terms of the sale, which were communicated at the time of purchase. We encourage customers to report any issues within the allotted warranty period so we can address concerns promptly.

Thank you for your understanding. Please let me know if you need anything else from us in this matter.

REMOVEDsaid that REMOVEDno longer works there so my notice did not count. I asked her why she didn't have that exemployee's client communications forwarded so there would be continuous service to her customers she said that didn't matter since I could've looked up other people in the company to call on my own. She actually said that in written email response to me. Currently I am being billed for 3 months of parking plus late fees.
Target Park US Inc.

Customer new we didn't receive her email and therefor her cancelation was not effective and choose to ignore this. Until the balance is paid, we cannot cancel the account. Customer is welcome to work out either a payment plan or a reduced payment but will have to make payment for the account to be closed.Thank you,REMOVED
Lori S

Date: 01/21/2025

This is unbelievable. I have a contract with Target Park USA. The cancellation clause says you must provide written notice of cancellation 30 days in advance and I did that on November 6, 2024 for a December 23, 2024 renewal so I did meet the contract specifications on cancelling my service. I never received anything from Target Park about any changes in communications. I received an email from REMOVEDon November 30, 2024 stating rates were going up and I answered her with the email chain from her terminated employee that I did, in fact, notify Target Park USA a full 47 days in advance. The Target Park USA manager, REMOVED, clearly could see that I notified her employee in good faith, but is choosing to do business in an unethical way because they know few people will challenge them legally and since they are not a regulated business like insurance or banking they get by with it. I will challenge.
Target Park US Inc.

complaints.text: Target Park USA does not have clear signage or clear payment processes. They arbitrarily charge whatever they feel like charging, again, with no clear signage or ticket prices. They cover their payment kiosks and signage, so drivers and parkers have no idea where to park and what to pay. They change payments without letting vehicle owners know about the fees. They arbitrarily change fees without letting people know and do not have correct signage. Target Park USA also discriminates against senior citizens, my parents who both received the ticket, as Target Park does not have attendants or signage listing that they own the lot or what the rates are; furthermore, they change fees for various phone users. The Target Park USA lots are intermingled with the free REMOVEDlots downtown and we saw many drivers and cars with tickets or those about to get tickets from Target Park USA as again, it was not clear what area was for Target Park USA and what were the free Ocean City, NJ parking lots. Target Park USA also ups its rates once they have them set which is an unethical and unfair business practice. They apparently have automated customer service emails where one cannot reach a live person, and we could not reach a live person with Target Park USA over the weekend. They upped the ticket price to $96 illegally in less than 48 hours (not even two business days as the incident occurred over the weekend) for 2 tickets that were supposed to be less than $40 each, again, from the information above it is evident we were not even supposed to get tickets as there was no Target Park USA signage by the free REMOVEDparking lots. Other drivers were/are so confused about the free vs. paid Target Park USA parking over the weekend at the lot as was evidenced by the many drivers and cars receiving tickets (some cars were getting tickets while others were not). Please refund this $72 for the two tickets for us due to Target Park USA's illegal, unethical and biased business practices. Thank you.
complaints.businessResponse:
Good afternoon,

 

There is signage on the lot with the pricing we are required to place this sign as per the town. The payment kiosks are covered because we don't take payments at the kiosks and we do not want customers to pay there and then receive a ticket. There are signs on the lot for customers to use the QR codes to make payments and so far, this is the first time we have had an issue with this. We do not make changes to payments. This is a seasonal lot. We have one price for summer and another price for the rest of the year and both are posted accordingly to the time of year. Our signage states the amounts that show on the app when scanning the QR code. We do not discriminate against anyone I am sorry you feel this way, but everyone needs to scan the QR code. Everyone gets charged the same when they scan the QR code given they have the same vehicle type and are staying the same amount of time on the same day. Also, it will depend on what time a person enters and leaves the lot. We only have two lots in OC, and both are signaled correctly with our signage and flags therefor everyone knows which lots are ours and which ones are not. We do not up our rates. Rates depend on days' time of year time of entrance time of exit and car make and model. There are a variety of things that go into parking rates in all companies that do parking. Customer personally emailed me and I explained to the customer to dispute ticket on the QR code on the ticket. Also, the area manager reached out to the customer. The ticket was not upped 48 hours after being processed as we can't manually do that. We have signage on the lot and the tickets were and are valid. Please pay what is owed as we have never offered free parking. 

 

Thank you,

Patricia

We advised them the oil was very low, and we put oil in and cardboard under car to check for leaks., no leaks found, and they requested to bring car back, they would check it out. We refused, we do not trust them or their mechanic, we were told to find a mechanic who deals with the warranty. Went to Nationwide Auto who works with the warranty to find out what's going on. By this time the car had used 6 quarts of oil, Nationwide diagnosed it as bad rings and needed a motor. REMOVEDtold them to do an oil consumption test. We did and within 700 miles it consumed 2 quarts of oil. Informed House of Cars and was told my $17,337.80 car was sold as is. I expected a good motor! Brought back to Nationwide to avoid further motor damage. Paid for all services requested by REMOVEDdue to them not covering it. House of Cars was informed through this whole process by us and Nationwide. Final request from REMOVEDwas for us to pay for engine break down and then would decide what they would cover. We declined that due to costing thousands and making us use miles for their tests. Cancelled warranty and informed House of Cars. Called House of Cars on a daily/weekly/monthly basis to get this taken care of and they do not return calls. Since moving into my apartment on August 1, 2026, I have experienced a recurring electrical safety issue involving Spectrum’s coaxial service. During thunderstorms, I have repeatedly observed visible electrical arcing along/around the coaxial cable inside my apartment. When this occurs, my Internet service drops and I do not consider it safe to touch the affected equipment until the storm passes. I work from home, so these repeated outages have also significantly disrupted my job.

A firewall connected to the network stopped functioning following one of these storm-related incidents and had to be replaced.

The electric utility inspected the service from the curb to the apartment and advised that interior/building-side conditions were outside its responsibility. Building management and its representatives investigated the issue and determined that the exterior coax grounding issue falls under Spectrum’s responsibility.

Most importantly, a Spectrum field technician has already inspected the system and told me that there is no grounding at Spectrum’s hub serving the property. Despite Spectrum being aware of this condition, the grounding issue has still not been corrected.

This is not simply an Internet reliability complaint. It is a recurring electrical safety hazard involving visible arcing during thunderstorms.

I am requesting immediate escalation to Spectrum plant/maintenance personnel to inspect and correct the grounding/bonding at the hub and associated coax infrastructure, verify the system is properly grounded/bonded, and provide written confirmation of the findings and corrective work performed. I also request a specific repair date and escalation contact rather than another routine in-home service visit.

This is very dangerous as electricity from lightning is entering my apartment.

On August 26, 2026, I visited a Spectrum store in REMOVED, REMOVED, returned all of my Internet equipment, and requested cancellation of my service because I was moving out that day.

August 26 was the last day of my existing billing cycle, and my next billing cycle began on August 27. However, Spectrum set my disconnection date as August 31, even though I had already returned all equipment and requested cancellation on August 26. I did not request or intend for my service to remain active until August 31.

Because the disconnection date was set to August 31, my account entered a new billing cycle beginning August 27, resulting in an additional charge of approximately $30.

I contacted Spectrum customer service and explained that I had returned all equipment and requested cancellation before the new billing cycle began. I asked Spectrum to review the cancellation date and adjust the resulting charge, but my request was denied.

I understand Spectrum's policy regarding non-prorated monthly billing. I am not requesting proration for a billing cycle that I intentionally entered. My concern is that I requested cancellation and returned all equipment on August 26, the final day of my existing billing cycle, but Spectrum assigned a later disconnection date of August 31, which caused an additional billing cycle to be charged.

I am requesting that Spectrum review the records from my August 26 store visit and remove or credit the approximately $30 charge resulting from the later August 31 disconnection date.

reviews.text: UPDATE: Management responded to this review telling me to call the resident office. Ive now called 7 times today with no answer. If we were still responsible for the apartment and our lease was active through September 8, why were workers allowed into and using our apartment before then?Problems happen at apartment complexes. reviews.name: Aaron P
reviews.text: After nearly eight years at Avery Point in REMOVED, I've watched the rent balloon with a steady stream of mandatory add-ons disguised as 'convenience.' Now they've rolled out a $70/month community Wi-Fi feeon top of a $35/month valet trash service (to walk my one trash bag a week 100 ft to the dumpster), a $5/month pest fee, a $1/month charge for credit reporting, a $4 utility billing fee, and a mysterious $5 community fee just for good measure. It's one thing to pay for what you actually use, but it's another to have these non-negotiable extras forced on residents. Bottom line: living here means paying for 'amenities' you never asked for. If you're considering moving to Avery Point or ANY IRT Property, you may want to think twice unless you're okay with surprise fees on top of your rent. There are plenty of places out there that don't nickel-and-dime residents this way.Finally... Before you write your canned response, REMOVEDalready reviewed these charges with the leasing office in the past (who said it was 100% corporate decisions), and the concern isnt a lack of explanation its the steady addition of mandatory fees for services I didnt request and dont have the option to decline. If these fees are truly meant to enhance convenience, residents should be able to opt out of the ones they dont use. Instead, theyre added automatically and folded into the cost of living here. After nearly eight years, its disappointing to see the community move in this direction. Im happy to discuss this further, but Id prefer that the conversation address the core issue: the growing number of non-optional add-ons that increase rent without adding meaningful value for many residents.

reviews.name: David P
reviews.text: In reference to the The Landings in REMOVEDwhich is an IRT Living property. The Landings leased an apartment to a family member site unseen. After moving to town, my family member was given a apartment that was literally disgusting. In appearance it was nothing like the one shown to me, the REMOVEDsystem was inoperative and it had a stench to it that was literally nauseating. In addition, the back screen door was inoperative. This was all at move in time. After "promising" all issues would be taken care of ASAP, including a deep clean, the apartment was in identical condition two days later. It was also not taken care of the next day or even the day after that. So, a total of 5 days after the agreed upon move in date, The Landings finally claimed all issues were resolved and it was move in ready. However, the stench in the unit was so repulsive, it caused nausea to multiple family members there to help move in. In addition to the physical issues with the unit, the staff at the Landings was incredibly unhelpful and rude. They refused to give specific answers to questions and refused to show other options that were available. They also failed to comply with the lease agreement. Eventually, my family member decided not to take the unit and found an alternative location. After multiple visits to the office and emails to corporate offices concerning a refund, there has been zero communication received regarding her refund. Put simply The Landings failed miserably to provide the service they were already paid for and now, given the complete silence from the corporate office and the leasing office, they intend to keep the money they have no legal right to. Given the complete lack of concern and abysmal customer service, IRT and The landings do not deserve an A+ rating. I wish a zero start rating was an option due to the completely unprofessional and disappointing experience with all aspects of the transaction.

complaints.text:
I requested a garage that a family member was vacating, sent emails confirming request on 7/2. I did NOT receive any acknowledgement of the request nor did we receive a contract addendum to review before execution. The family member ultimately returned the garage remote on 7/13 based on a lack of response from management and advised the leasing office that we would no longer be needing the garage; 30 minutes later we received a contract and discovered that our account had been charged for the garage on 7/10 and the charge was back dated to 7/3. Furthermore, in reviewing our account ledger we discovered that a carport parking space that was accepted for free as a lease renewal incentive had been charged to our account for several months. My wife immediately sent an email to the Property Manager formally advising that the garage was no longer needed, requesting the garage fee be removed from our account, addressed the monthly carport fee which was supposed to be free and and officially rejected / declined the garage addendum. We no longer need or want the garage, have not and do not have access to the garage since the former lessee returned the remote directly to the office and we did not sign the addendum agreeing to the terms. Our resident portal is still showing the July fee for the garage now that Aug rent has billed we see that we are still being charged for the garage and the carport resulting in nearly $300 in inaccurate fees preventing us from being able to pay that true and contractual balance due on our account. We have called the leasing & corporate offices and left messages that have not been returned, sent texts and emails with no response, and visited the office during normal business hours only to find the office closed. If the adjustments are not made immediately we will be forced to pay incorrect fees in order to avoid a late fee. There is NOT a contract addendum for the garage and we've communicated we don't need it now.
Customer Answer

Date: 08/04/2026

To Better Business Bureau,


I am writing to update you on Complaint ID REMOVED. The billing discrepancies regarding the garage fee and the carport charge have been fully addressed and resolved by the business.


The incorrect charges have been removed from our account ledger, and our balance is now accurate. As a result, I wish to mark this complaint as resolved and closed.
Thank you for your assistance in resolving this matter.


Best regards,
REMOVEDIce

complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for reaching out. REMOVEDBilling Change: As part of a community-wide utility update, we are transitioning cable billing to be managed through Xfinity/REMOVEDon behalf of residents. Each resident was provided proper written notice of this change in the form of a lease addendum, which required your signature to confirm review and acceptance of the update. To ensure residents were not financially disadvantaged by this change, we compared each resident's prior service cost to the new billing amount. Where a resident's previous cost was lower than the new charge, we applied a one-time credit to cover the difference through the remainder of their current lease term. At renewal, residents will be automatically enrolled in the updated billing structure going forward.


Payment Method / Bank Account Fee: Regarding the $7.95 fee charged for paying rent via bank account/debit, this fee is associated with the payment method selected through our resident portal and is disclosed as part of the available payment options. Residents may choose among available payment methods, each of which may carry different processing fees depending on the provider.

We understand your frustration with the added cost, but the change was communicated in advance and formally acknowledged via signed addendum, consistent with standard lease amendment procedures.

complaints.text: I signed a lease online with REMOVEDliving, for an apartment unit to be moved into on July 17th. complaints.text: Date of transaction: April 30, 2026 After putting in a 90 day notice to move out of my apartment as renewal letters were mailed out two months early by the parent company, REMOVED, I was assured on more than one occasion by employees in the leasing office that a move out date of April REMOVEDwas confirmed as alright and without any penalties. One employee even picked up the phone and called the finance office at REMOVEDto confirm. I wish I had had the office manager confirm but there is no way to call the office and have anyone pick up the phone to assist their residents and the manager leaves early. The robot answering calls from humans has proven to be a big problem and I'm bearing the brunt of it. I went in personally after work, I checked more than once and I was assured by two different leasing agents that no penalties were showing with a move out of April 30. I paid $100 to have my apartment cleaned in late April and it was "move-in ready" according to the maintenance manager who toured it with me. I did everything I knew to do as I had bought a house due to the renewal letter being mailed out in January vs. March in my specific case, closed on it and needed to move. I would have stayed if I had not been told moving out in April was okay. Now the finance office, REMOVED, has charged me $1,000 for "turning my keys in early". Yet I did what I was told was alright to do. And I would have done it differently if I was told different. And now, instead of trying to resolve it or do the right thing, they have, yet again, a bot contacting me and have turned it over to collections. I was either lied to by somebody and feel like I was hoodwinked because I would have done whichever way they said was the right thing to do. I worked to increase my credit to buy a house and now this which will ding my credit and I don't appreciate being inconsiderate way I was treated. And after 7 years of being a good, dependable tenant, they still don't know my name.
