Our team retried these payments via REMOVEDon August 26, 2026; REMOVEDtransactions typically take 13 business days to clear or fail, which impacts the timeline for resolving the restriction.

The customer contacted our support team on August 25 and again on August 27, 2026. A full explanation was sent to the customer August 29, 2026. User has not responded to 8/29 email: 

Hello Arber,

Thank you for reaching out! After reviewing your Aeropay account, it is currently restricted due to declined payments from 8/15/2026 and 8/16/2026, for a total of $1,250.00 to Polymarket. The payment retry was made on 8/26/2026. Please note that this process takes approximately 2-3 business days to complete; weekends and holidays are not included in this time frame. Once that payment is successfully resolved, your access will automatically be restored across the network; this includes withdrawals.


At this time:
The reason for the restriction has been identified and communicated to the customer (insufficient funds on the three original payment attempts).
The retried REMOVEDpayments were processed on August 26 and are subject to the standard 13 business day clearing window.
We are continuing to monitor the account to confirm the REMOVEDretries clear successfully, at which point the restriction will be lifted automatically  and full withdrawal access restored.
We have reached out directly to the customer with this explanation and will follow up promptly once the REMOVEDtransactions clear t

complaints.text: I am requesting assistance because I have been unable to get a response from AeroPay regarding an account issue.The REMOVEDaccount is currently registered under my mothers name, REMOVEDJean REMOVED, but I am the person trying to use the account. My email address associated with the account is REMOVEDand the phone number associated with the account is REMOVED. The bank account I need to connect is legally under my name, REMOVED, not REMOVEDJean REMOVEDthe legal names do not match, I have not initiated any transfers. I want to resolve this before sending any funds to avoid verification issues, failed transfers, or account restrictions.I have contacted AeroPay through their support email, their social media support, and their escalation email requesting assistance, but I have not received a response. I am willing to provide any government-issued identification or documentation necessary to verify my identity.I am not requesting any monetary compensation. I simply want AeroPay to respond to my support request and either update the account to my correct legal name if their policies allow, or provide instructions on how to close the current account and create a new account under my own legal name.
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for the opportunity to respond. Aeropay has reviewed this matter and takes customer support concerns seriously.

Our records indicate that the customer initially contacted REMOVEDon Friday, July 17, 2026, regarding updating the account information to reflect the correct legal name. We responded on Monday, July 20, 2026 the next business day requesting the documentation necessary to verify the customer's identity and process the requested account changes.

After receiving the required documentation, we completed our review and successfully resolved the customer's request that same day (7/20/26).

Based on our records, Aeropay responded within our normal support timeframe, requested the information necessary to complete the request, and resolved the matter once the required documentation was received. We can also confirm that the customer has since been able to successfully complete a withdrawal using the updated account information.

We appreciate the opportunity to address this concern and consider this matter resolved.

complaints.text: I was trying to withdraw money from a Daily Fantasy Sports App, the app requires me to use Aeropay in order to withdraw funds directly from them, I had my spouse fill in information for me while I had to tend to duties around the house, she mistakenly put in her details and when I tried to withdraw my funds were locked due to delinquent activities, me trying to resolve this naturally went to aeropay email and sent several emails throughout the span of a week and a half but have received no response from anyone, all I want to do it fix the account details and or delete the account so I can properly proceed to use the service to take out my funds from the REMOVED
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for the opportunity to respond.

When a bank account is connected that doesn't match the name on the account holder's profile, our system automatically places a freeze on the account as a standard fraud prevention and compliance measure.

We were only able to locate one email from the user from their email address on file, which we responded to, and did not receive a reply back. We're happy to look into this more if the user can point us to specific dates or forward any additional emails so we can track them down.

In the meantime, we've already disconnected the unauthorized bank account and removed the freeze. The account is now fully restored, and the user can either connect a bank account in their own name to proceed with the withdrawal, or reach out to us directly to update the account holder information.

We appreciate the user's patience and are here to continue assisting. We encourage the user to follow up with us directly.

complaints.text: My payment account was disabled on REMOVED. Support is not responding to emails. Please provide a way to settle this issue so my payment account can be reactivated
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for the opportunity to address this complaint.

The account was disabled because the customer disputed (charged back) four payments to Kalshi made between 6/19/2026 and 6/23/2026, totaling $8,100. This is a standard fraud-prevention measure triggered automatically when payments are disputed through a bank rather than resolved with us directly.

We also want to note that the bank account associated with the four disputed transaction has been used for REMOVEDtotal since it was connected on 5/6/2026, none of which were disputed apart from the four currently in question. This bank account has been continually used for both deposits and withdrawals since connection. Additionally, on 6/23/2026, prior to the customer's bank providing our system with R08 return codes later that day, the customer completed a withdrawal of $1,300 to the same bank account from which the disputed transactions originated. We share this for context as it may be relevant to resolving the dispute.

The customer first reached out on 7/4/2026, which is outside of our business hours. We apologize for our delayed response (7/9/26), as we're currently experiencing higher-than-normal support volume.

We have reached out to the customer to request more information around their reason for the disputes. Further communication is necessary to arrive at a resolution.

If the disputes were filed for non-fraud reasons, such as service dissatisfaction: once the customer confirms with us that the disputes have been formally lifted by their bank, we will retry the four payments. The account can be reactivated once the payments successfully process, as the customer had already received platform credit on Kalshi for those payments and the balance must be settled prior to re-activation.

If the disputes were filed due to fraudulent activity, we are unable to resolve outstanding balances stemming from fraud claims without confirmation from REMOVEDthat a fraud investigation has been completed and unauthorized

complaints.text: I am filing this complaint because Aeropay failed to properly handle an unauthorized $82.00 charge and demonstrated inadequate fraud protection and customer support.On May 29, 2026, a fraudulent charge from The Daily Green appeared on my Aeropay account. I immediately notified Aeropay that:I was not at the merchant on that date The only time I visited was May 45, when Aeropay failed multiple times I paid cash, and no Aeropay transaction should exist Aeropay responded by telling me the charge was pending and that they could not help until it posted. They instructed me to wait and contact the merchant myself an inappropriate response for a fraud REMOVEDexpected, the charge posted, exactly as I warned. Only after it posted did Aeropay ask me for proof and again direct me back to the REMOVEDbank ultimately refunded the money, but Aeropays handling of the situation was slow, dismissive, and demonstrated no meaningful fraud prevention, leaving me to resolve the issue on my own.
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for the opportunity to respond.

Aeropay takes reports of unauthorized transactions seriously and reviewed this matter based on the information available to us, including the transaction details and communications received from the customer.

Our records show that the disputed transaction was originally authorized on April 29, 2026, and was submitted for settlement by the merchant on May 29, 2026. The submission of an authorized transaction for settlement is initiated by the merchant and is not something Aeropay controls.

When the customer contacted REMOVEDon May 29, the transaction was still pending. At that stage, we were unable to reverse or refund the payment because the transaction had been submitted for processing but had not yet settled. We advised the customer to contact the merchant regarding the order and explained that additional action could be taken once the transaction had posted.

After receiving the customer's inquiry after business hours on May 29, 2026, we responded on June 2, 2026, which was within two business days. After the customer requested escalation, we followed up on June 3, 2026, requesting additional information needed to investigate the reported unauthorized transaction. We did not receive any further response to that request, which limited our ability to complete our review.

We understand the customer was dissatisfied with this experience and appreciate the opportunity to clarify the steps taken by our team. Aeropay followed its established review procedures and responded based on the transaction's processing status and the information available at the time.

At this time, the transaction has been disputed and the funds have been returned to the customer through their financial institution.

complaints.text: This company processes payments for the betting app Slips. This company has held my money ($100), for several days. They claim the bank account I added was closed, and my money would be returned to my Slips balance, it has REMOVED$100 is nowhere to be found and I cant get an answer or resolution to this matter. This is a simple taska simple transfer. It is now my belief that Slips and Aeropay attempt to make this process so difficult and frustrating, that the customer just give up. Well, Im not stopping until I receive my money.
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for bringing your concerns to our attention. We understand how frustrating it is when a withdrawal does not go through as expected.

After reviewing this matter, we confirmed that the withdrawal was returned because it was sent to a bank account that had been closed. The receiving bank returned the transaction with an R02 return code, which indicates that the account is closed. REMOVEDdoes not hold funds when a withdrawal is returned for this reason.

Once we became aware of the issue, we confirmed that you successfully connected a new checking account to your REMOVEDprofile and advised you to contact Slips regarding your account balance. REMOVEDfacilitates the transfer of funds between participating financial institutions but does not hold or manage user balances maintained on our partner platforms. As a result, we do not have visibility into or control over the balance displayed within your Slips account.

Additionally, Aeropay is unable to initiate withdrawals on behalf of users or reissue funds held by our partner platforms. To receive your funds, the withdrawal will need to be initiated again through your Slips account using your newly linked bank account. If the balance has not yet been restored within Slips, their support team is best positioned to review your account and make any necessary adjustments.

If you continue to experience payment processing issues after retrying the withdrawal, we are happy to work with Slips to investigate any Aeropay-related processing concerns.

We appreciate the opportunity to clarify our role and remain available to assist with any Aeropay-related payment processing questions.

complaints.text: I am filing this complaint regarding my experience with AeroPay and the difficulties I have encountered while attempting to withdraw my funds.I received an Additional Verification Needed message when trying to withdraw funds through my account. The withdrawal is associated with my Kutt account via REMOVED. During the account setup process, I mistakenly used a wrong phone number. Once I realized the error, I worked to correct the information and contacted both Kutt and AeroPay to update my account details.Despite correcting the phone number issue and communicating with both companies, I continue to receive verification-related errors and remain unable to access my funds. I have repeatedly reached out to customer support seeking clarification on what specific documentation or information is required to complete the verification process, but the issue remains unresolved whilst they keep assuring me that it has been resolved . Its been 3 weeks now and my money has been held captive by Aeropay My primary concerns are:1. Lack of clear communication regarding the exact reason for the verification failure.2. Continued inability to withdraw my funds despite correcting the identified account information issue.3. Delays in resolving the matter despite multiple attempts to work with customer support.I am requesting that REMOVEDprovide a clear explanation of the verification issue, specify any additional documentation required, and promptly resolve the restriction so I can access my funds.I have acted in good faith to correct the account information and comply with all verification requirements. I am seeking a fair and timely resolution to this matter.Thank you for your attention to this complaint.
complaints.businessResponse:
Thank you for bringing this matter to our attention. We take all customer concerns seriously and appreciate the opportunity to address your experience.We sincerely apologize for any frustration caused by the delays in resolving this matter.

However, we would like to provide important context regarding the nature of this issue.

1. Aeropay serves as a payment processor for REMOVEDand does not hold or restrict customer funds.
2. The verification errors experienced are a direct result of the account being registered with identity information that is not associated with the individual initiating the withdrawal. Our verification systems are designed to protect customers and comply with financial regulations, and they are unable to process transactions when the account credentials provided do not align with the verified identity of the account holder.

After thorough review by the technical teams at both Aeropay and Kutt, it was determined that the verification integration could not be successfully reset. Once introduced, these discrepancies created compounding issues that could not be corrected within our systems.

As a result, Aeropay recommended that REMOVEDdisburse the funds through an alternative payment method. REMOVEDsubsequently made the decision to issue a full refund of the account holder's deposits directly, and the case has been closed on their end.

complaints.text: The original transfer took place on 4/21/26 for $100. My account was disabled after the $100 was returned and I was still able to add an additional $275 from my debt card and bet which is how I won over $3000. I am filing this complaint regarding PrizePicks and its payment processor, Aeropay, for restricting access to my account funds while failing to provide a reasonable way to resolve a balance issue.Over a week ago, a $100 transfer from my bank account to PrizePicks was returned/declined. Since then, my PrizePicks account has been restricted from withdrawals. However, my account currently has a balance of over $3,100, and PrizePicks continues to allow deposits and betting activity while preventing me from accessing my winnings.I have repeatedly attempted to resolve the matter directly with both PrizePicks and Aeropay. I submitted the requested verification documents and have contacted support multiple times through email and chat. Despite my efforts, I continue receiving delayed or generic responses without any actual resolution or timeframe REMOVEDconcern is that there appears to be no reasonable or accessible process for resolving the alleged $100 balance issue, even though the company is currently holding significantly more money in my account than the disputed amount. I even requested that the $100 simply be deducted from my existing account balance, but no meaningful assistance has been provided.This situation has caused significant financial hardship because I am unable to withdraw funds that belong to me while the companies continue delaying resolution. I believe consumers should have access to timely support and a fair process for resolving account/payment disputes, especially when large balances are being held.I am requesting immediate review of my account, resolution of the outstanding balance issue, and restoration of my ability to withdraw my funds.
complaints.businessResponse:
Aeropay appreciates the opportunity to respond to this complaint and clarify the circumstances surrounding this matter.

Initial Payment Issue (R03 return):
The users initial bank transfer was returned by the receiving bank with an R03 return code, indicating that the account information provided could not be validated at the time of processing. As a result, the associated account was restricted from certain capabilities pending resolution of the outstanding balance and verification of updated banking information.

Account Reconciliation and Processing Delay:
During the resolution process, updated banking details were submitted through a separate Aeropay profile rather than the original account. Because account history, transaction activity, and verification records are tied to the original profile within our system, additional review was required to identify and reconcile both accounts before the balance could be reprocessed.

Support Interactions:
The user also opened multiple support tickets across email and chat regarding the same matter. This resulted in duplicate outreach from multiple team members and contributed to a repetitive support experience while the issue was being reviewed.

Role in Withdrawal Processing:
Aeropay does not hold, manage, or control user balances maintained within the PrizePicks platform, including winnings or withdrawal balances. Aeropays role is limited to facilitating bank-to-bank payment transfers between a users financial institution and the merchant platform. While alternative payout methods may be available through the merchant, Aeropay does not process withdrawal transactions for accounts with unresolved outstanding balance issues related to prior returned payments.

Resolution:
Aeropay has since reconciled the duplicate accounts and transferred the users verified banking information to the original account associated with the declined payment. The retry payments have successfully cleared, the outstanding balance has been resolv

complaints.text: I have an account with PrizePicks, which is an online sports betting app. My bank is connected to Aeropay. My bank is through REMOVEDOn the night of February 8, 2026 my Prizepicks account was hacked into. Two separate transactions of $300 and $390 ($690 total) were taken from Chase REMOVEDI IMMEDIATELY reported this to my bank, Prizepicks, and Aeropay. REMOVEDcompensated me. However, Prizepicks and Aeropay refused to allow me to withdrawal from the REMOVEDOn March 10, 2026, REMOVEDruled in my favor. For several weeks I tried to withdrawal existing funds out of my Prizepicks account but was not allowed to. Then on the morning of April 11, 2026 Aeropay without warning took $690 from my Prizepicks account even though they have been told SEVERAL times in no uncertain terms that this case was ruled in my favor. They do not communicate via telephone and instead rely on this ridiculous live chat. I am asking to immediately be refunded my $690 and be allowed to withdraw funds out of my prizepicks again! This is beyond ridiculous. Every time I try and resolve the matter with Aeropay or Prizepicks, they give me the runaround. I have attached both statements. One from March 2026 indicating a ruling in my favor and one from April 2026 indicating that Aeropay took $390 and $300 out of my prizepicks REMOVEDIn addition, REMOVEDwill NOT allow me to withdrawal from my bank REMOVEDBeyond ridiculous how they continue to give me the runaround like this!! I really need this $690 to pay bills!
complaints.businessResponse:
We understand the seriousness of this situation and appreciate the opportunity to clarify.

This user was a confirmed victim of fraud, as verified by PrizePicks, and this was documented on the users Aeropay profile upon notification.

Aeropay facilitates bank-to-bank transfers between a users financial institution, such as REMOVED, and the merchant, but does not hold or control funds within the PrizePicks platform. The transactions in question were identified as fraudulent and remained declined. However, because Aeropay does not have visibility into merchant-side balance adjustments, PrizePicks later modified the users in-app balance without our awareness, which created a discrepancy with the previously declined transactions.

Once this was identified, we worked to correct the issue and ensure the fraudulent transactions were properly resolved.

Resolution: The previously declined fraudulent transactions have now been fully resolved, the users Aeropay account is in good standing and able to transact, and PrizePicks is in the process of restoring the users in-app funds.

We recognize the frustration this caused and are working with PrizePicks to improve coordination in confirmed fraud cases.

complaints.text: I play fantasy sports. They use aero pay as a payout method. Prize picks put me off the app with no explanation. But aero pay controls the money. I had over $1,000 on the app. And they closed my account to where I couldn't even look at my account. Sent me $27. I tried to pull all the money off for 2 days before they shut out my account. But aero pay wouldn't allow me to redeem MY MONEY now I'm out a thousand dollars and nobody has any answers. I wrote aero pay. They wrote back then immediately blocked me. This needs to be pushed to proper authority. At this point its criminal. All these complaints of theft in BBB and no authority have been contacted? Prize picks and aero pay are both scamming people.
complaints.businessResponse:
We understand the concern raised and appreciate the opportunity to provide clarification. Aeropay does not hold or manage user funds within third-party platforms. Any balance referenced in this complaint is maintained by the merchant, PrizePicks. Aeropays role is limited to facilitating secure bank-to-bank transfers when initiated by the user or the merchant, and we do not have visibility into or control over funds held within a merchant account.

Our records indicate that we were in communication with the complainant and confirmed that a refund in the amount of $27 was being processed. For questions related to any remaining balance or account access, the complainant will need to work directly with PrizePicks, as they manage the user account and associated funds.

At a certain point, we were unable to continue the correspondence after the tone of the communications no longer aligned with our support guidelines. Aeropay remains committed to maintaining a respectful and constructive support environment and is happy to re-engage to assist with any transfer-related questions that fall within our scope.

We encourage the complainant to reach out to PrizePicks for further support regarding their account and any remaining funds. Aeropay remains available to assist with any questions related to our services.

complaints.text: 7/9/2024. New name of business Anti-Aging Northwest. Met with naturopathic physician REMOVEDre bio-identical hormone refill request with current labs. She renewed scripts, with a followup in 6 months ( 1/15), told her I had pain in lower right abdominal region, which she said put castor oil wrap. All occurred within 20 minutes and I left.I attempted to reach out to office and REMOVEDNickel a short time later, to complete a form that I could give to my insurance carrier, to help offset the costs of the hormone creams. I knew the office did not BILL insurance, but thought a few minutes filling out a form for me, was not too much to ask, since I paid out of pocket $200 for a very short visit. I was never responded to, reaching out to both naturopathic physicians as well as front desk gal. Finally, after asking for a super bill of the visit, which is legally obligated, the front desk gal said oops, she was pregnant and she guessed she missed my inquiries. She then stated that the office won't assist their clients with the paperwork. I was not asking for insurance billing, just a small note to enable me to get the creams from insurance company. Very difficult to get anyone to communicate at this office.Since the castor oil wrap did not relive the pain, I went to a Nurse Practitioner in a REMOVEDwho did a pap exam and sent me to the hospital for a pelvic ultrasound. REMOVEDdeficiency was causing uterine lining buildup, cramping, and subsequent uterine bleeding. I was put on a higher dosage of REMOVEDand problem abated.Recently, as Dr. REMOVEDwanted me to come back in to charge another $100 for a hormone check, I told her of my adventures and that I had found a much superior solution, with a provider who charged me $15 for an office visit, happily filled out the forms, and was conscientious in tracking down the problem with my cramping and bleeding, which could have been a serious issue. She responds very promptly.Emailed REMOVEDabout this.

complaints.text: Autoban garage sells car parts. I purchased some parts from him to use on my car. I sent him money through REMOVEDfriends and family as he requested. The amount was $700. When the product showed up, i noticed that it was not the exact product that i ordered. I sent him a picture of this and he immediately called me. He told me that this product would still work and that i should use it anyways since the other one may not be in stock. He said it would work just fine. So i took his advice and went to install it on the car. However, the product would not fit correctly. I messaged him about this aswell and he told me that it was cut to fit. He said he had contacted the manufacturer of the part and they verified that it had to be cut in order to fit. So i once again followed his advice and cut it until it fit. Once it was finally in i noticed another problem. It was too different from what i had originally ordered and would not work with the other parts on the car as needed. I reached out and told him that it would not work to which he told me it was too late and i had already cut it so it couldnt be returned. I was not able to tell that it would not work until it was in, i could not have forseen this. Also, never once was there any disclaimer that cutting the parts to fit them or even installing them would make it so that they could not be returned if they did not work properly. He now refuses to work with me on this and wont give me a refund or the original product that i ordered. After all of this, i reached out to some other retailers of this product. I have now found out that this part is not cut to fit as he stated and is not meant for my kind of car, contrary to what he had said. All of the misinformation he gave me on the product led to me losing $600 and having a car that doesnt drive. At this point i would just like my money back.
complaints.businessResponse:
Hello, my name is REMOVEDBan, i am responding to this complaint.  I am the owner of autoban garage. Responding to this complaint, id like to state that the transaction was done via REMOVEDfriends and family due to being a personal transaction to selling REMOVEDa part at cost value.  Drift HQ is the dealer for the manufcatured part that was drop shipped to REMOVED.  The dealer stated that those were the parts he ordered, and actually spent time to provide PDF images of the manufactured part to show him. Autoban garage is a third party, and is not involved in any reimbursement even if possible. In this case, i myself REMOVEDBan, took the liberty of reaching out on his behalf to see what could be done, since he modified the incorrect part, and regardless of needing modification or not, these parts are advertised as non OEM , non DOT approved parts.  They are meant for the racetrack and may require custom modification per each application.

This is a response just to clear the situation, but essentially REMOVEDis an entitled customer wherever he shops. this is likely not the first invalid complaint he has submitted.  REMOVEDBan or AutoBan Garage has not recieved any product or item back at all to recieve any refund.  Refunds are not garunteed ever as stated on REMOVEDin the terms and agreements.

REMOVEDhas reached out to me personally and now is attempting to attack a different business that has nothing to do with this personal transaction via REMOVEDfriends and family. please reach out REMOVEDfor a folder of screenshots if required, from both dealer and distributor email chains.

 

thank you

articles.title: Celebrating integrity: International Torch Awards for Ethics announce 2026 winners
articles.summary: The International Association of Better Business Bureaus (IABBB) announces the winners of the 2026 International Torch Awards for Ethics.

image.alt: International Torch Awards for Ethics logo

articles.h1: Celebrating integrity: International Torch Awards for Ethics announce 2026 winners
articles.deck: The International Association of Better Business Bureaus (IABBB) announces the winners of the 2026 International Torch Awards for Ethics.
paragraphs: The International Association of Better Business Bureaus (IABBB) announces the winners of the 2026 International Torch Awards for Ethics.

Presented annually since 1996, the BBB International Torch Awards for Ethics recognize businesses in North America that maintain outstanding dedication to upholding ethical business practices and promoting trust in the marketplace. Companies were evaluated against four criteria including the Character of the organization’s leadership; if and how an authentic Culture is being fostered; the company’s transparent relationship with its Customers; and the impact the organization is making in the local Community. This year’s competition was exceptional, with more than 130 entries from outstanding businesses that have already earned the prestigious Torch Award in their respective regions.

Four businesses are receiving recognition for their outstanding commitment to leadership character and organizational ethics. Winners will be honored at a special event in Denver, CO on September 16, 2026. The 2026 winners are:
Category 1, 1-10 employees: ONE NINE Architects
Category 2, 11- 99 employees: Roxi & Co
Category 3, 100- 499 employees: Core Bank
Category 4, 500+ employees: Hy-Vee

“Ethical leadership is the foundation upon which lasting trust is built,” said Jonathan Liebert, Interim CEO of the International Association of Better Business Bureaus (IABBB). “The International Torch Awards for Ethics recognize organizations that go beyond simply doing what is required and make integrity, transparency and accountability part of who they are. This year’s honorees represent the very best of our business community, demonstrating that success and strong values can go hand in hand. We are proud to celebrate their leadership and the example they set for businesses across North America.”
About the winners

Category 1 (1-10 employees) ONE NINE Architects ONE NINE Architecture is a design-driven architecture and interior design firm creating thoughtful and distinctive spaces rooted in collaboration, creativity, and purpose. The firm believes in the transformative power of design to strengthen communities, demonstrating that commitment by dedicating 10 to 30 percent of its professional services pro bono to individuals, communities, and nonprofit organizations that might otherwise lack access to high-quality, thoughtful design.
Category 2 (11-99 employees) Roxi & Co

Roxi & Co. is a locally owned pet retailer and pet services company based in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. The company specializes in high-quality pet food and supplies, as well as professional dog waste cleanup services. Roxi & Co. is committed to building lasting relationships with its customers, investing in its team, supporting local animal rescues and community organizations, and finding meaningful ways to give back.

Category 3 (100-499 employees) Core Bank Core Bank is a locally owned financial institution built around the belief that strong businesses create strong communities. Headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, with locations throughout the Omaha and Kansas City metropolitan areas, Core Bank combines relationship-driven guidance and local expertise with responsive, forward-thinking financial solutions that help businesses grow, invest confidently, and build long-term stability.

Category 4 (500 or more employees) Hy-Vee Hy-Vee is an employee-owned corporation operating more than 540 business units across nine Midwestern states, with annual sales exceeding $14 billion. The supermarket chain is known for its commitment to quality, variety, convenience, healthy lifestyles, culinary expertise, and superior customer service. The company's commitment to its employees, customers, and communities has earned national recognition, including being named among the top grocery stores in America by USA TODAY and to PEOPLE magazine's list of 100 Companies That Care. The award-winning companies were selected by an independent panel of business and ethics experts all dedicated to maintaining business ethics in the marketplace.

articles.title: BBB Scam Alert: Don't be fooled by "free" gas and grocery card postcards
articles.summary: As the cost of living continues to strain many household budgets, it's no surprise that consumers want to take advantage of legitimate savings opportunities. Scammers are using the U.S. mail to lure people with promises of free gas and groceries.

image.alt: person using card to pay for gas at tank

articles.h1: BBB Scam Alert: Don't be fooled by "free" gas and grocery card postcards
articles.deck: With the cost of groceries and fuel continuing to strain many household budgets, it's no surprise that consumers are eager to take advantage of legitimate savings opportunities. Unfortunately, scammers know this too, and they're increasingly using the U.S. mail to lure people with promises of free g
paragraphs: With the cost of groceries and fuel continuing to strain many household budgets, it's no surprise that consumers are eager to take advantage of legitimate savings opportunities. Unfortunately, scammers know this too, and they're increasingly using the U.S. mail to lure people with promises of free gas and grocery gift cards.

Better Business Bureau (BBB) has recently received multiple reports through our BBB Scam Tracker page from individuals who received postcards claiming they qualified for valuable gas and grocery cards and vouchers.

A Northwest Georgia resident was among many people who recently reported their experience with this type of mailing from “AAPP.” The resident reported that he received a postcard claiming that $309.64 of gas and grocery vouchers was being held in his name.

He noted that he did some research and was taken to BBB’s Scam Tracker page to learn more. However, others who didn’t do their homework weren’t as fortunate. Instead, they found that when attempting to claim what sounded like valuable vouchers, they got tricked into spending money. Several reported additional unauthorized transactions appeared on their accounts. There’s been no indication that any vouchers were received.

Here’s what one woman shared: “Sister received a postcard from AAPP, Presorted 1st class mail from Tampa phone #. Postcard stated she was eligible for gas & grocery cards. She agreed to the $5 processing fee, then immediately after they took another $46. Total dollars lost: $51.”

The use of a costly postcard can make the offer appear authentic but also shows just how much money can be earned by taking advantage of unsuspecting individuals. These scams often target thousands of consumers and even modest unauthorized charges can quickly add up for criminals.

The postcards may include official-looking barcodes, tracking numbers, expiration dates, and customer service phone numbers to create a false sense of credibility. Some even use urgent language to pressure consumers into responding quickly before they have time to research the offer. These can include: "Limited time offer," or "Final notice."

In addition to groceries or gas, these types of mailings may claim to offer rebates or shopping rewards. Recipients are usually instructed to call a phone number or visit a website to claim their reward, and as noted in the example above, callers are usually asked to pay a fee, which may be referenced as a small processing, activation, shipping, or handling fee—often around $5—to receive hundreds of dollars in gift cards or vouchers.
Once payment information is provided, one of several things may happen:
Additional unauthorized charges appear on the consumer's account.
The consumer is unknowingly enrolled in a monthly subscription program.
The promised gift cards never arrive or low-value coupons or promotional materials are received instead.
The company becomes difficult—or impossible—to contact for refunds.
Your BBB recommends taking these precautions:

Remember that legitimate prizes don't require you to pay first. If someone asks for a processing fee, activation fee, shipping charge, or any other upfront payment before you receive your reward, consider it a major warning sign.

Research the company independently. Don't rely solely on the information printed on a postcard. Research the company's name along with words like "BBB," "reviews," or "scam." Visit BBB.org to check the company's Business Profile, customer reviews, and complaint history.
Never provide payment information under pressure. If you’re told you must act immediately, slow down. Legitimate companies won't pressure you into making an immediate payment.

Watch your bank and credit card statements carefully. If you've already provided payment information, review your accounts for unauthorized charges and report suspicious transactions to your financial institution immediately.

articles.title: BBB Tip: Decluttering? Tips for selling your used items online
articles.summary: Online marketplaces, like Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace or Poshmark, make it easy to sell your gently used clothing, furniture, home items, or electronics. Here are BBB's tips for avoiding scams while successfully making sales.
articles.h1: BBB Tip: Decluttering? Tips for selling your used items online
articles.deck: Updated November 3, 2025 with updates to tips.
paragraphs: Updated November 3, 2025 with updates to tips.
The start of a new year is a great time to clean out your home and organize your living spaces.
But what should you do with the gently used clothing, furniture, exercise equipment, home items, or electronics that you aren’t using anymore?
Fortunately, online marketplaces, such as Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, eBay, and Poshmark, make it easy to sell without even leaving your home.
What you'll learn:
How to safely sell your gently used items online or locally, including choosing the right platform, pricing, and creating effective listings.
Ways to protect yourself from scams, safeguard personal information, and use secure payment and shipping methods.
Alternatives to selling, such as swapping or donating items, and tips for decluttering and organizing your home.
That said, there are a few perils to selling used items online. To avoid the dangers and to successfully make sales, BBB recommends the following tips.
How to stay safe when making online sales

Choose an appropriate platform. When planning to sell items online, Nerdwallet recommends you “think about what you’re selling and the type of online marketplace that suits it.” There are dozens of online marketplaces to choose from, but many of them focus on a specific kind of used goods, such as electronics or designer clothing. Before you create an account with a marketplace, make sure it is a good fit for the kind of goods you want to sell.

Check the platform's refund and dispute policies. Understand how the platform handles refunds, disputes, and chargebacks. Be aware of timeframes for reporting issues and gather any required documentation or evidence that may be needed if a buyer files a dispute.

Use secure payment methods. Stick to payment methods offered by the platform, as they often have security measures in place. Avoid accepting checks or wire transfers, as these are common methods scammers use to manipulate sellers.

Know the worth of your items and price appropriately. To determine the value of an item you want to sell, try searching for similar items on the site where you plan to list. On auction sites, look at completed sales and pay attention to the selling price rather than the minimum bid price. If you are selling an item that was never used and is still in its original packaging, remember that technically it is still coming to the buyer second-hand, so you’ll need to charge a little less than the original retail value if you want to make a sale.

Get appraisals for high value items. If you are selling jewelry made with precious metals or stones, get an official appraisal before you list or sell the items. Keep in mind that jewelers may give you a lower price quote as they intend to make profit on a resale. If you are in possession of antiques or artwork that is worth over a thousand dollars, consider getting a written opinion on the item’s worth from a professional appraiser. This will give you a better idea of the price you should set and how much insurance you need to cover the sale.

Make a quality listing. Without a good listing, you may not sell your item. Make sure the images are clear and accurately show the item’s color, form, and other key details. You’ll also want to include specific measurements and detailed written descriptions that inform buyers of any flaws the item may have, no matter how small. Make it clear that the price you set takes the flaws into account. Finally, use search engine words in your item description that accurately describe the item, its aesthetic, and its use to attract buyers who are actively looking for what you are selling.
Consider the timing. List seasonal items ahead of relevant holidays or seasons (e.g., winter coats in early fall, exercise equipment in January) to maximize buyer interest.

Prepare items for sale. Before you pack your item for shipping or prepare it for being picked up by the buyer, clean it thoroughly. If you are planning on selling multiple items online and want to keep buyers coming back, put some love into your packaging as well. Wrapping the item in tissue paper and including a thank you note can go a long way towards creating a returning customer.

paragraphs: Updated November 4, 2025 with bonus tips and updated references.

Scaling and sustainability will continue to be the main focus for any small business owner. There are many ways to achieve revenue growth, attracting top talent, instilling a healthy culture, delighting customers, and so much more.
What you'll learn:
Ten strategic New Year’s resolutions to help your small business grow sustainably, strengthen customer relationships, and attract top talent.
How to align your company’s goals with trust, transparency, and purpose to build long-term brand loyalty.
Ways BBB Accreditation and Standards for Trust can help your business stand out in a competitive marketplace.
Here are 10 business New Year's resolutions that you may want to consider for a successful 2026.

Continue building a strong digital footprint – Aside from having a website, ensure you build a solid content marketing strategy that will help you create valuable content pieces that will drive engagement and sales. Read BBB’s tips on improving your website and how to use social media to find opportunities for growth.

Promote your business consistently – Rather than waiting for major holidays to push larger promotions, find ways that you can creatively promote your business throughout the entire year. This ensures that you stay top of mind for your target customers. Check out BBB’s tips on how you can expand your current offerings for growth.

Personalize the entire buyer journey – The days of communicating “at” your target audience, hoping they will buy from you, are now a thing of the past. 81% of customers prefer companies that offer a personalized experience. Therefore, personalize the buyer journey by offering products/services based on your customers’ purchase behavior and complementary items they can also consider.

Embrace an effective technology stack – From social media to email marketing, know that every piece of technology you leverage to communicate with your customers must effectively impact your business goals. More specifically, here are five tips your business can start using today.

Reduce costs – Save money wherever you can without compromising quality. Many businesses fail due to inadequate financing and low revenue. Reducing cost doesn’t mean that you focus merely on just overhead. There are various ways you can cut back spending while pushing for growth. Here’s how small businesses can cut costs without sacrificing growth.

Have a positive workplace culture – Your employees are the lifeblood of your company. Every day, they contribute to the success of your business by supporting its mission. However, the most crucial role that your employees play is in shaping your firm's culture. From the quality of the people you hire to the loyalty of your consumers, corporate culture is critical to practically every facet of your business's long-term success. In fact, according to a study by Duke University, more than 94% of executives stated that a distinct business culture is important to business success.

Push customer reviews - Reputation can mean everything, especially for a small business owner trying to attract and retain customers. According to the 2024 Edelman Trust Barometer, 63% are more likely to purchase new products on behalf of a brand they fully trust. You want to tell customers that your business is trustworthy, ethical, and transparent – and what better way to illustrate that story than through online customer reviews? Check out Power of Customer Reviews on Small Businesses to see how BBB ensures accuracy and transparency with its review program.

Exercise transparency - Operating with transparency builds relationships that turn curious browsers into buyers and buyers into raving fans. Always be transparent, from admitting missteps and correcting them to inviting your customers to engage with you online and through social media. Authentic interaction with your clients goes a long way to building customer trust.

Be purpose-driven - By understanding what is most important to your customers, you can leverage their values within your company collateral, which can further illustrate that you’re not just a “for-profit” company, but you care about your community. In other words, you are a purpose-driven company pushing for a larger impact than just making sales. Purpose-driven brands see success both among their customers and their employees. Share moments on social media that demonstrate your purpose and mission, and don't be shy to show how your brand is committed to helping make a difference.

Establish trust - Building trust is crucial to earning your customers' trust. When making a purchase, buyers have many options at their disposal. Customers have been able to be more attentive when picking which brands to support as a result of this accessibility. The best method to increase client loyalty and assure your company's success is to build a company based on trust and integrity. Giving your business a step up over the competition is always something to desire; aiming for BBB Accreditation is a valuable way to do this. Accreditation requires the utmost trustworthiness, customer respect, and integrity, which can help your business stand out.
Bonus resolutions for 2026

articles.title: BBB Tip: Need to get in shape? BBB has tips for joining a gym
articles.summary: Before you sign on the dotted line, get the most from a gym membership with these tips from BBB.
articles.h1: BBB Tip: Need to get in shape? BBB has tips for joining a gym
articles.deck: If your goal is to lose weight, get in better shape, or improve your overall health, deciding to join a gym may be the first step. However, don't just sign up at the first gym you see or visit. Before signing on the dotted line, research all options first! Get the most from a gym membership by consi
paragraphs: If your goal is to lose weight, get in better shape, or improve your overall health, deciding to join a gym may be the first step. However, don't just sign up at the first gym you see or visit. Before signing on the dotted line, research all options first! Get the most from a gym membership by considering these tips from BBB:

Determine your fitness goals. Determining your goals in advance will help you select a facility that is most appropriate for you. Consult with your physician before embarking on a new fitness regimen, especially if there are medical conditions that might be a concern.

Know your budget. Besides the monthly fee, check for hidden costs such as enrollment fees, cancellation fees, or charges for additional services like classes or personal training. Ensure the gym fits your budget long-term.

Figure out your priorities. What is most important to you? Will a convenient location and extended hours help you stick to your fitness plan? Will a variety of equipment or classes keep you motivated? Do you work out while traveling and prefer a chain with numerous outlets? Determine your top priorities before you start shopping around.
Check BBB.org. Read what previous customers have to say, and see how the businesses respond to complaints. This information may help you narrow down the list of gyms you want to tour in person.

Take a tour. Make sure the gym has the equipment, classes, and trainers you need or expect. Pay attention to things that are important to you, whether it’s the cleanliness of the showers or the availability of Wi-Fi. Ask questions and make sure you understand all the rules. Ask about busy times, wait times for equipment, whether classes require pre-registration, availability, and cost of trainers, etc. Ask how the gym staff is maintaining the cleanliness of the facilities.

Consider online and app-based access. Some gyms offer virtual classes, streaming options, or mobile apps for at-home workouts. These can add value, especially if you may not make it to the gym every day.

Ask questions about limited free trials. Gyms often give a one-week free pass for potential members; this is a great way to see if the gym is a good fit for you. Try the gym at different times to see how crowded it is and whether there is a wait for certain equipment. Check out classes if they are offered.

Don’t feel coerced. Do not give in to high-pressure sales tactics to join right away. A reputable gym will give you enough time to read the contract thoroughly, tour the facilities, do some research, and make an informed decision.

Calculate the true costs. Gyms often use special introductory offers to encourage new members, but the price could go up more than you budgeted once the initial period is over. Make sure you understand what the regular monthly fees will be and what they include.

Understand membership freeze options. Ask if the gym allows you to pause your membership if you are unable to attend for a period due to illness, travel, or personal reasons. This can be a valuable option if your schedule is unpredictable.

Look for flexibility in membership types. Some gyms offer membership tiers or pay-as-you-go options. This can be beneficial if you're unsure about committing to a long-term contract or only need limited access.
Ask about member discounts and perks. Some gyms offer discounts for students, families, or corporate partnerships. Be sure to ask if there are any additional perks or discounts available.

Understand the terms. Read the contract carefully before signing. Make sure that all verbal promises made by the salesperson are in writing. What matters is the contract and the terms within it, so don’t just take a salesperson’s word for it. What happens if you move or the gym goes out of business? Will the membership renew automatically at the end of the term? What is the cancellation policy and under what circumstances?
Go to BBB.org to look up a business, file a complaint, write a customer review, report a scam, and read additional tips.
Read more about BBB Accreditation Standards and BBB Standards for Trust.
